rows.expected: (a) BASECONVERT(255, 10, 16) returns FF (15.12.3 r1 admits an unsigned integer literal below base 11); (b) equal bases raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION with checking ON; (c)/(d) COMP and numeric-edited argument-1 rejected or EC; (e) 16.5 rejected as non-integer base; (f) base 20 diagnosed at compile per 4.2.2 para 3
rows.actual: (a) compiles clean, run aborts 'CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: intrinsic string argument BoundNumericLiteral', exit 127; (b) EQ=[FF] + NOT-RAISED with checking ON; (c) COMP=[FF]; (d) EDIT=[FF]; (e) FRAC=[255] (16.5 truncated to 16); (f) compile exit 0, zero diagnostics
rows.derivation: 15.12.3 r1 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30206): 'shall be a usage display or national data item or literal, and, if the base specified in argument-2 is less than 11, shall also be an unsigned integer data item or literal. Argument-2 and argument-3 shall be positive nonzero numeric integer literals or data items with unequal values in the range 2 to 16.' So 255 is a legal argument-1 at base 10 and must yield a value; equal bases / binary usage / numeric-edited / 16.5 all violate r1, and 15.3 (line 29561: 'the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') requires the EC when checking is ON.

DISPLAY "BC=[" R "]"' compiles with ZERO diagnostics and the run dies with 'Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: COBOL.NET: a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: intrinsic string argument BoundNumericLiteral' at _PRG_RFSPOT4.__Dispatch, exit 127 -- leg (a) of the record, on a legal argument shape 15.12.3 r1 admits below base 11. So a GREEN test does pin this arm, and the fix shape the prober describes (per-function admission, not a blanket route) is the right one -- feedback_green_test_can_hold_a_gap_open applies. Not a false STILL-LIVE.

rows.expected: §15.13.3 r1 'Argument-1 shall be a positive integer.' A negative literal (-5), a negative data item (PIC S9(4) VALUE -5) and a non-integer literal (5.5) are all non-conforming argument-1 shapes; the compiler must diagnose them (it already owns the vocabulary — COBOLNET1627 fires for a non-integer DATA ITEM).

FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5.5, 8) -> NONINTLIT=00000101 (truncated to 5), exit=0. NV PIC S9(4) VALUE -5 -> NEGITEM=00000000, exit=0. Only the non-integer DATA ITEM leg is screened: NF PIC S9(3)V9(2) -> 'error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER argument-1 is a numeric data item with digits to the right of the decimal point, which ISO §15.3 type 6 does not admit ... (§15.13.3 r1/r2)', exit=70.
rows.derivation: Read §15.13.3 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30239 — '1) Argument-1 shall be a positive integer.' The rule has TWO conjuncts, POSITIVE and INTEGER. The recorded note said only the numeric CLASS was screened; the landed PB40 work added the INTEGER conjunct for data items (§15.3 type 6). Neither conjunct is applied to a LITERAL, and the POSITIVE conjunct is applied nowhere. Expected therefore = a diagnostic on each of the three shapes; observed = a value.

rows.mechanism: The §15.3-type-6 argument screen in IntrinsicArgumentRules/CheckArgumentClasses models argument-1 as a CLASS-plus-integrality predicate over a bound DATA ITEM; it has no value-domain (sign) channel at all, and the literal path never reaches the integrality arm — so the POSITIVE conjunct of r1 is written down nowhere and the INTEGER conjunct has a data-item-only arm.

rows.expected: §15.13.3 r2 'Argument-2 shall be a positive nonzero integer.' Argument-2 = 0, = -3, = 4.5, and a data item holding 0 or -3 are all non-conforming and must be diagnosed.
rows.actual: All ACCEPTED silently. (5, 0) -> ZEROLEN=00000000, exit=0 (a zero-length boolean result, MOVEd into PIC 1(8) and zero-filled). (5, -3) -> NEGLEN=00000000, exit=0. (5, 4.5) -> NONINTLEN=01010000, exit=0 — argument-2 was truncated to 4, producing a FOUR-position result '0101' left-justified into the 8-position receiver. Data-item forms: LN PIC S9(4) VALUE -3 -> NEGLENITEM=00000000; LZ VALUE 0 -> ZEROLENITEM=00000000. No diagnostic at any leg.
rows.derivation: Read §15.13.3 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30241 — '2) Argument-2 shall be a positive nonzero integer.' Three conjuncts: POSITIVE, NONZERO, INTEGER. §15.13.4 r1 makes argument-2 the returned item's length in boolean positions, so a zero/negative length has no defined returned value at all. Expected = a diagnostic on each shape; observed = a silently mis-sized result.

rows.actual: TYPE-NAME (ZSL02A): rejected at COMPILE time - `error COBOLNET1639: 'TN' is not defined ...` plus a cascading `error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH argument-1 is a numeric literal, which 15.14.3 r1 does not admit`, which MISDESCRIBES a type-name as a numeric literal. Legal source rejected. REF-MOD (ZSL02B): compiles with ZERO diagnostics, then `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of a reference-modified argument (runtime length, 15.14.4)`. FIXED HALVES: the NEGATIVE side is now a compile-time diagnostic - ZSL02D `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(12345)` -> `error COBOLNET1627 ... (ISO 15.14.3 r1)` (was a zero-diagnostic compile + runtime throw); and the SIBLING `FUNCTION LENGTH(X(1:3))` now ANSWERS 3 (ZSL02C), so the ref-mod arm was fixed on the LENGTH side only.
rows.derivation: 15.14.3 rule 1, quoted from specs/ISO_COBOL.md: "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal, a based entry, a type-name, or a data item of any class or category." A type-name is named explicitly, so 7 (the type declaration's byte width) is owed. A reference-modified operand is admitted under the 'data item of any class or category' arm because 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 makes reference modification 'create a unique data item that is a subset of the data item referenced by identifier-1' and GR6 gives it 'the same class, category, and usage', so it IS a data item; with a literal length the answer folds to 3. 15.14.4 rule 1 - "The returned value is an integer that is the length of argument-1 in number of bytes" - fixes the values at 7 and 3.

rows.expected: Re-derived independently from the rule text I read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30366 -- 15.16.3 r2: 'The value of argument-1 shall be greater than zero and less than or equal to the number of positions in the national program collating sequence.' The identity national sequence has 65536 positions, so EVERY value outside 1..65536 is an incorrect argument value and 15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist -- fatal with checking ON. Critically, that is true of the TRUE value, not of any narrowed image of it: a magnitude >= 2^63 that an unchecked (long)(Int128) cast would alias INTO the window (including one that aliases onto the LEGAL maximum 65536), and a NEGATIVE magnitude that aliases onto a positive in-window ordinal, must all be rejected.
rows.actual: Every wrap-shaped magnitude is now rejected with its TRUE value printed in the message, on four separate argument channels: rfa1 CHAR-NATIONAL(PIC 9(20) 18446744073709617152 = 2^64+65536) -> 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument 18446744073709617152 is outside the range the function can represent (ISO 15.3)', exit 1; rfa2 (PIC S9(20) -18446744073709551550 = -(2^64)+66) -> same fatal EC naming -18446744073709551550, exit 1; rfa3 (arithmetic expression BIGN + 0) -> same fatal EC naming 18446744073709551682, exit 1; rfa5 (non-identity ALSO-shrunk national PCS, 2^64+65535) -> same fatal EC, exit 1. Controls: rfa4 CHAR-NATIONAL(66) -> CTRL-66=[A] and ORD(CHAR-NATIONAL(65536)) -> CTRL-MAX=065536, exit 0 (no over-rejection). rfa6 with checking OFF -> CHECKOFF=[ ] (the 15.3 one-space default) then CONTINUES -- NOT the aliased ordinal-66 character 'A', which proves the lossy narrowing itself is gone rather than merely fenced by a guard placed in front of it.
rows.derivation: 15.16.3 r2 read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30366 (quoted above) plus 15.3's closing paragraph ('If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'). The recorded defect was NOT 'the bound is wrong' -- the note itself verified the bound -- it was that IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt's '(long)(Int128)' narrowing is unchecked in C# and wraps modulo 2^64, so the guard never saw the true value. The refuting question is therefore not 'is 2^64+66 rejected' but 'is the guard now applied to the TRUE value on every channel and at every sign', which is what the five probes below test.

XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL NAT-A. SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C". / CHAR-NATIONAL(18446744073709617151) | rfa6.cob (RF1632F): same 2^64+66 value with NO checking directive. Command for each: E:\CobolSharp\src\Cobol.Net.Cli\bin\Debug\net10.0\cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run
variations: ALIAS-ONTO-A-LEGAL-VALUE magnitude (the discriminating axis the prober's 2^64+66 could not be): 2^64+65536 = 18446744073709617152 narrows to exactly 65536, the LEGAL maximum, so a surviving post-narrowing guard would have ACCEPTED it silently -- rfa1 rejects it naming the full 20-digit value
SIGN axis, untouched by the prober: PIC S9(20) VALUE -18446744073709551550 = -(2^64)+66 narrows to +66, an in-window ordinal -- rfa2 rejects it naming the negative value
ARGUMENT-EXPRESSION channel (prober varied only data item vs literal): FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (BIGN + 0), an arithmetic expression rather than a leaf operand -- rfa3 rejects

NON-IDENTITY collating path crossed with the wrap magnitude (prober tested the ALSO bound only at 65535/65536, never with a wrapping value): ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"B" ALSO N"A", N"C" + 2^64+65535 -- rfa5 rejects
CHECKING-OFF result: rfa6 returns the 15.3 one-space default, not the aliased character -- the narrowing is gone, not merely guarded

rows.refute-evidence: CONFIRMED FIXED. Five new probes along four axes the prober did not vary (alias-onto-legal-max, negative sign, arithmetic-expression channel, non-identity path x wrap) plus the checking-off result all agree with the prober. The strongest attempted overturn -- 2^64+65536, which narrows onto the legal maximum and would slip past any guard still sitting downstream of the cast -- failed to overturn: the diagnostic prints the full 20-digit value, so the range test now sees the Int128. RESIDUE, not an overturn: the record demanded a WHOLE-CHANNEL sweep ('every i argument rendered through AsInt': CHAR, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER, BASECONVERT, the FORMATTED-DATE/-TIME offsets, the DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD windowing trio). The prober swept CHAR only; the other functions are outside this row's rule and belong to their own rows -- I did not re-probe them and they are not evidence for or against this row.

rows.derivation: Re-read from specs/ISO_COBOL.md myself. 15.17.3 r1: 'Argument-1 shall be in integer date form.' 15.5.2 (read at line 29824): 'A value in integer date form is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600, in the Gregorian calendar. It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671.' 0 is not greater than zero, -5 is not a positive integer, 3067672 exceeds the stated maximum. The sibling functions PROVE this compiler can enforce exactly that predicate: rfd1/rfd2 show FORMATTED-DATE aborting on the same values 0 and -5 with 'argument 0 outside 1..3,067,671 (§15.5.2)'. So the guard exists and COMBINED-DATETIME simply does not call it - a false STILL-LIVE is excluded.
rows.probe: rfn1.cob (PROGRAM-ID RFN1): 01 WS-ID PIC S9(9) VALUE 0. 01 WS-SEC PIC 9(5) VALUE 45296. 01 R PIC Z(9)9.9(5). >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON / COMPUTE R = FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) / DISPLAY 'ZERO=' / MOVE 3067672 TO WS-ID / repeat / MOVE -5 TO WS-ID / repeat / DISPLAY 'NOT-RAISED'. Command: cobol.exe rfn1.cob --std 2023 -o rfn1.dll --run
variations: CROSS-FUNCTION CONTROL (new): the identical 15.5.2 predicate on the identical values IS enforced for FORMATTED-DATE - rfd1.cob (argument 0) and rfd2.cob (argument -5) both abort 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): FORMATTED-DATE argument 0 / -5 outside 1..3,067,671 (§15.5.2)', exit 1. The divergence is therefore a missing call site, not an unimplementable rule.
rows.mechanism: The 15.5.2 value guard exists as a shared runtime helper and is wired into the string-returning FORMATTED-* arm but not into COMBINED-DATETIME's numeric fold (integerDate * Pow10 + secUnscaled), which has no guard prologue - the two-arm dispatch shape with one arm hardened.

rows.derivation: 15.17.3 r2: 'Argument-2 shall be in standard numeric time form.' 15.5.5 (read at line 29840): 'If the LEAP-SECOND directive with the OFF phrase is in effect, the value shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400.' I additionally validated the OFF-mode premise against 7.3.17 GR1 ('If the LEAP-SECOND directive is not specified, a LEAP-SECOND directive with the OFF phrase is implied before the first compilation unit') and GR5 ('When OFF is specified or implied, a standard numeric time form value shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400') - both read verbatim at lines 3999 and 4018. So the admissible interval is [0, 86400): 86400 is the first illegal value and -1 is below the floor. LO=143950.99999 shows the negative argument-2 borrows a whole day from the DATE component.

rows.derivation: 15.23.3 r5 (read at '#### 15.23.3'): 'If argument-3 is omitted, the function shall be evaluated as though the following were specified for argument-3: (FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4)))'. That is an IDENTITY, so the two forms must agree in one execution whatever the clock reads. The expression is legal COBOL - 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 permits reference modification of a function-identifier that references an alphanumeric function, and 15.21.1 makes CURRENT-DATE alphanumeric - so it must also parse. rows.mechanism: Binder, IntrinsicBinder.BindFindString: argument-3 is bound through BindArgOperand over the whole arithmeticExpression alternative and the only screen reachable is the 15.3 type-6 numeric-scale test on a bound field operand, so a scaled LITERAL and every arithmetic EXPRESSION bypass it; IntrinsicRenderer.IntArg -> AsInt then emits (long)(CobolNum.Rescale(..., Truncation)) and the truncation is invisible. r3 needs its own shape arm, as the note says.

rows.expected: r1 imposes two independent requirements - LITERAL-ness and CLASS membership in {national, alphanumeric}. Every legal spelling of a national or alphanumeric literal shall be ACCEPTED (including the hexadecimal-alphanumeric and hexadecimal-national FORMATS and a 13.10 constant-name); a boolean literal, an identifier and a figurative constant shall be REJECTED.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo2.cob draws 'error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE argument-1 is of class boolean; ISO §15.3 requires class alphanumeric, alphanumeric (numeric-edited) or national (§15.38.3 r1)' for B"0101", and 'error COBOLNET1517: FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE argument-1 shall be a literal date/time format' for a PIC X(20) identifier, exit 70. VARIATION 1 (hexadecimal-alphanumeric): rfb1.cob's FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE(X"595959592D4D4D2D44445468683A6D6D3A7373") is ACCEPTED and prints HEXFCD=[2026-08-09T09:26:19]. VARIATION 2 (figurative constants): rfb2.cob's FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE(SPACE) draws COBOLNET1517, as do FORMATTED-DATE(ALL "YYYYMMDD") and FORMATTED-DATETIME(ZERO). VARIATION 3 (13.10 constant-name): rfb3.cob's FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE(FMT-CD) with '01 FMT-CD CONSTANT AS "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss".' compiles and runs. VARIATION 4 (the zero-length literal): rfp2.cob's FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE("") draws COBOLNET1631 (the r2 content rule) and NOT COBOLNET1627 - the class screen correctly declines to attribute it here.
rows.derivation: 15.38.3 r1 read at line 31320: 'Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal.' 8.3.3.2 Format 2 is the hexadecimal-alphanumeric FORMAT of the alphanumeric literal (line 5115) and 8.3.3.5 Format 2 the hexadecimal-national format (line 5316), so X"..." and NX"..." are literals of the two classes r1 names and refusing either would reject legal COBOL. A figurative constant is not a literal, so it must be refused. 13.10.4 GR1 makes a constant-name substitute its literal, so it must be accepted. 8.3.3.2's zero-length literal is a legal ALPHANUMERIC literal, so it satisfies r1 and may be refused only under r2 - the discriminator that separates a correct class screen from one that rejects on length.
rows.probe: rfo2.cob (boolean literal + identifier, three functions); rfb1.cob (hexadecimal-alphanumeric literals for FORMATTED-DATE / -DATETIME / -CURRENT-DATE); rfb2.cob (SPACE, ALL "...", ZERO); rfb3.cob (constant-names across five functions); rfp2.cob (the zero-length literal). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: LITERAL-FORMAT AXIS - the prober varied literal CLASS (boolean/national/alphanumeric) but never the FORMAT within a class. The hexadecimal-alphanumeric format is accepted and decoded (HEXFCD renders a real timestamp), so the screen keys on the literal's Category rather than on its lexical spelling.
FIGURATIVE-CONSTANT AXIS - SPACE, ZERO and ALL "..." are each rejected by COBOLNET1517. The prober never drove these; they are the shapes closest to a literal that r1 does not admit.

ZERO-LENGTH LITERAL - the discriminator the original note explicitly warned about ('do not attribute it here'). "" draws the r2 diagnostic and not the r1 class diagnostic, so the two rules are separately enforced rather than collapsed.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB1.md + kb/Work/PB19.md + kb/Work/PB48.md (all landed) - re-verified: the diagnostic reports the literal's own Category ('class boolean') and the r1 and r2 screens fire independently, which is exactly the per-function, per-position, category-aware shape those notes describe.

rows.expected: Both directions shall hold: a national or alphanumeric literal written in ANY legal spelling - including a 13.10 constant-name, a hexadecimal format and an 8.8.3 concatenation - shall be ACCEPTED, and a boolean literal shall be REJECTED.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfb3.cob's 'MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE (FMT-D WD) TO RZ' with '01 FMT-D CONSTANT AS "YYYYMMDD".' prints CFD=[19950215], exit 0; rfo2.cob's 'MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE (B"1010" 143951) TO R' draws 'error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE argument-1 is of class boolean; ISO §15.3 requires class alphanumeric, alphanumeric (numeric-edited) or national (§15.39.3 r1/r3)'. VARIATION 1 (family sweep): rfb3.cob drives constant-name arguments through FIVE functions in one program - FORMATTED-DATETIME (CFDT=[19950215T123456]), FORMATTED-TIME (CFT=[123456]), FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE, INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE (CIOFD=[000143951]) and FORMATTED-DATE - all accepted, exit 0. VARIATION 2 (national spellings): rfb4.cob accepts N"YYYY" & N"MMDD" (NCAT=[19950215]), the hexadecimal-national NX"0059005900590059004D004D00440044" (NHEX=[19950215]) and N"YYYYMMDD" & N"Thhmmss" into FORMATTED-DATETIME (NCATDT=[19950215T123456]), each delivered into a PIC N(24) receiver. VARIATION 3 (figurative): rfb2.cob rejects SPACE and ALL "YYYYMMDD" with COBOLNET1517.
rows.derivation: 15.39.3 r1 read at line 31359: 'Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal.' 13.10.4 GR1 makes a constant-name substitute its literal unconditionally and 13.10.3 SR2 permits it 'anywhere that a format specifies a literal of the class and category of constant-name-1', so refusing one rejects legal COBOL. 8.3.3.2 Format 2 and 8.3.3.5 Format 2 make X"..." and NX"..." formats of the alphanumeric and national literal respectively, and 8.8.3 makes a concatenation expression a literal - all three must bind. 8.3.3.4 types B"1010" class boolean, which r1 does not name, so it must be refused. A figurative constant is not a literal at all.
rows.probe: rfb3.cob (constant-names across five FORMATTED-*/INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE functions); rfb4.cob (national concatenation, hexadecimal-national, national concatenation into FORMATTED-DATETIME, all into PIC N receivers); rfo2.cob (boolean literal at argument-1 of three functions); rfb2.cob (figurative constants). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: FAMILY-SWEEP AXIS - the prober's sweep evidence was UPPER-CASE/TRIM/LENGTH (the note's own collateral list). rfb3.cob instead sweeps the FORMATTED-* family itself, where the over-reject originally lived, and all five bind. The channel fix reached the whole family, not one function.

NATIONAL-SPELLING AXIS - the prober used a NATIONAL CONSTANT only. rfb4.cob adds the hexadecimal-national literal and the national concatenation expression, both accepted AND typed national (they deliver into PIC N(24) and DISPLAY-OF renders them), so the fix restored every spelling of the national class rather than the one form it happened to run.
FIGURATIVE-CONSTANT AXIS - the nearest-neighbour shapes that must still be refused are refused, so the accept half did not overshoot into non-literals.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R01.md (status: landed) for the over-reject half - re-verified across five functions rather than one; kb/Work/PB1.md + kb/Work/PB19.md (COBOLNET1627, category-aware) for the under-reject half.

rows.expected: (A) The 15.5.2 value guard shall be reached for every out-of-range argument-2 - the LOW end (zero and negative) as well as the high end and values past 2^63 - and 15.3 rule 14 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be SET, which means the abort with checking on AND the implementor-defined result with checking off. (B) An alphanumeric operand and a non-integral numeric operand shall both be rejected.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo1.cob (P18 * 100 + 67 = 18,446,744,073,709,695,567 = 2^64 + 143,951) aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument 18446744073709695567 is outside the range the function can represent (ISO §15.3)', exit 1 - reported at full width, so no modulo-2^64 wrap. rfo2.cob rejects an alphanumeric argument-2 and a PIC 9(6)V99 argument-2 with the two COBOLNET1627 messages naming 'argument-2'. VARIATION 1 (LOW end, never probed): rfd1.cob (argument-2 = 0) aborts 'FORMATTED-DATE argument 0 outside 1..3,067,671 (§15.5.2)' and rfd2.cob (argument-2 = -5) aborts naming -5, both exit 1. VARIATION 2 (the other half of 15.3 rule 14): rfd3.cob runs all four illegal shapes - 0, -5, 3067672 and the 2^64 wide value - with checking OFF and prints OFF-ZERO / OFF-NEG / OFF-HI / OFF-WIDE all as spaces followed by REACHED-END, exit 0; no abort, no wrap to 19950215, and the implementor-defined result (A.1 item 90) is returned. VARIATION 3 (literal operand, not just a data item): rfp2.cob rejects FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYMMDD" "143951") with COBOLNET1627 naming argument-2 class alphanumeric.
rows.derivation: 15.39.3 r3 read at line 31365: 'Argument-2 shall be a value in integer date form.' 15.5.2 supplies the value half in full: 'a positive integer ... It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671.' The phrase 'greater than zero' makes 0 and every negative value violations exactly as 3067672 is - and the LOW end is the half neither the note nor the prober ever ran, so a guard written as a bare upper-bound test would have passed both and failed here. 15.3 type 6 supplies the class half: 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified'. 15.3 rule 14 requires the exception condition to be SET; with checking off the standard licenses the implementor-defined result, so returning spaces and continuing is the required complement of the abort, not a second defect.
rows.probe: rfo1.cob (the 2^64 value, checking ON); rfd1.cob / rfd2.cob (argument-2 = 0 and -5, checking ON); rfd3.cob (all four illegal shapes, checking OFF); rfo2.cob and rfp2.cob (alphanumeric item, alphanumeric literal, fractional item). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: LOW-END AXIS - 15.5.2 has two bounds and every probe on record tested only the upper one. Zero and -5 both abort with the correct citation, so the guard is the full interval 1..3,067,671 and not an upper-bound test.

CHECKING-OFF DISPOSITION - the prober measured only the abort. With checking off all four illegal values yield the implementor-defined empty result and execution continues to REACHED-END; critically the 2^64 value yields spaces rather than the old 19950215, proving the wide-value fix is in the value channel and not merely in the abort path.

LITERAL vs DATA ITEM for the class screen - the prober screened a PIC X item; an alphanumeric LITERAL in argument-2 is rejected too, so the screen is on the argument's category and not on its being a field reference.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB22.md (landed) for the unchecked narrowing; kb/Work/PB40.md (landed) for the 15.3-type-6 integrality arm; kb/Work/PB19.md (landed) for the per-position table the diagnostics ride on. All re-verified: the wide-value message and the 15.5.2 message are distinct and correctly scoped, and the low end reaches the 15.5.2 one.

rows.expected: A national literal argument-1 shall be accepted AND shall give the function a national type in every spelling of the national class; a boolean literal shall be rejected; a figurative constant shall be rejected.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo2.cob's 'MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME (B"0101" 153569 45296) TO R' draws 'error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME argument-1 is of class boolean; ISO §15.3 requires class alphanumeric, alphanumeric (numeric-edited) or national (§15.40.3 r1/r3/r4/r5)' plus the r2 format diagnostic, exit 70. VARIATION 1 (national CONCATENATION, a spelling never probed): rfb4.cob's 'MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME (N"YYYYMMDD" & N"Thhmmss" WD WS) TO RP' with 01 RP PIC N(24) compiles, runs and prints NCATDT=[19950215T123456] through DISPLAY-OF. VARIATION 2 (13.10 constant-name argument-1): rfb3.cob's FORMATTED-DATETIME(FMT-DT WD WS) with an alphanumeric constant prints CFDT=[19950215T123456]. VARIATION 3 (figurative): rfb2.cob's FORMATTED-DATETIME(ZERO WD WS) draws COBOLNET1517. VARIATION 4 (national result into an alphanumeric receiver): rfo4.cob's MOVE of FORMATTED-DATETIME(N"YYYYMMDDThhmmss" ...) into PIC X(40) draws COBOLNET0819.
rows.derivation: 15.40.3 r1 read at line 31402: 'Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal.' 15.40.1's table (line 31386) - 'Alphanumeric|Alphanumeric, National|National' - makes a national argument-1 give the function a NATIONAL type, which is what this row was graded on; 14.9.25.3 SR10 then bars the result from an alphanumeric receiver. The refutation risk was that the type might be attached to the recognised token N"..." rather than to the literal's category, in which case a concatenation of national literals would fall back to alphanumeric and slip past the MOVE screen. It does not: the concatenated form delivers into PIC N(24) and the plain form is refused by PIC X(40) in the same tree.
rows.probe: rfb4.cob (national concatenation argument-1 into PIC N(24)); rfb3.cob (alphanumeric constant-name argument-1); rfb2.cob (figurative ZERO); rfo2.cob (boolean literal); rfo4.cob (national result into PIC X). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: NATIONAL-SPELLING AXIS - the prober used the literal N"..." only. A CONCATENATION of two national literals also yields a national-typed result (it lands in PIC N(24)), so the type follows the literal's category through the 8.8.3 fold rather than being keyed on a token.
CONSTANT-NAME AXIS - a 13.10 constant-name argument-1 binds for THIS function too, so the class screen was not built by narrowing what counts as a literal.
FIGURATIVE-CONSTANT AXIS - ZERO is refused, so the accept half does not extend past literals.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB15.md (landed) for the result-type table and kb/Work/PB1.md + kb/Work/PB19.md for the category-aware class screen; re-verified on a literal spelling that only a category-based implementation can get right.

rows.expected: 15.3 type 6 makes an arithmetic expression a legal argument-2, so a conforming program using one shall COMPILE and produce the right date under EVERY arithmetic mode the targeted edition offers, and on every intrinsic sharing the integer-argument channel; the class and integrality of argument-2 shall be screened.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rff2.cob under OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. compiles and runs with expression arguments throughout; rfo2.cob rejects an alphanumeric argument-2 and a PIC 9(6)V99 argument-2 with COBOLNET1627 naming argument-2. VARIATION 1 (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD - the OTHER standard mode the original note named and every probe held fixed): rff1.cob at --std 2014 (STANDARD was removed in 2023, correctly diagnosed by COBOLNET0807 at --std 2023, so 2014 is the edition where the axis exists) prints STD-EXPR=[19950215T123456] and STD-OFF4=[19950215T123456+0500] with only the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning, exit 0. VARIATION 2 (the sibling sweep the note demanded and no probe ran): rff2.cob drives arithmetic expressions through SIX intrinsics on the shared integer-argument channel under standard-decimal - DOI=[19950215] (DATE-OF-INTEGER), DAYI=[1995046] (DAY-OF-INTEGER), CHAR=[A] (CHAR), FT=[123456] (FORMATTED-TIME), FD=[19950215] (FORMATTED-DATE), IOD=[000143951] (INTEGER-OF-DATE) - all compile and all values correct.
rows.derivation: 15.40.3 r3 read at line 31406 with 15.3 type 6: 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified.' That sentence makes WS-A + WS-B a legal argument-2 under every arithmetic mode, so emitting uncompilable output for it is an internal failure on conforming source; it equally makes a PIC 9(6)V99 item and an alphanumeric item illegal. The original note stated the defect as '(and STANDARD)' and named DATE-OF-INTEGER, CHAR, BASE-CONVERT, FORMATTED-DATE and FORMATTED-TIME as sharing the channel - both are axes the prober left fixed, and either could have carried an unfixed arm. Values re-derived: 100000+43951 = 143951 = 1995-02-15 (confirmed by INTEGER-OF-DATE(19950215) = 143951 in the same program), 40000+5296 = 45296 s = 12:34:56, ordinal day 046, CHAR(66) = 'A'.
rows.probe: rff1.cob (OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD. run at --std 2014 and --std 2023); rff2.cob (OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. with expression arguments to DATE-OF-INTEGER, DAY-OF-INTEGER, CHAR, FORMATTED-TIME, FORMATTED-DATE and INTEGER-OF-DATE); rfo2.cob (alphanumeric and fractional argument-2 for FORMATTED-DATE and FORMATTED-DATETIME). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std {2014|2023} -o <n>.dll --run
variations: ARITHMETIC-MODE AXIS - ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, the second mode the note named, works at 2014 where the clause is legal; and the compiler correctly refuses the clause at 2023 with the Annex E.2 item 21 citation, so the axis is closed in both directions.

SIBLING-INTRINSIC SWEEP - the note called the missing Dec arm 'a PATTERN' over the whole integer-argument channel. Six intrinsics on that channel now accept an arithmetic expression under standard-decimal and return correct values, so the landing was the channel and not this function.
ARGUMENT-POSITION AXIS extended - rff1.cob puts expressions in argument-2, argument-3 AND argument-4 of one call under a standard mode; the offset renders +0500 from OF1 + OF2 = 300.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md (status: landed) for the Dec-blind seconds/integer channel, kb/Work/PB40.md for the integrality screen, kb/Work/PB22.md for the wide-value half; re-verified across both standard arithmetic modes and six sibling intrinsics.

rows.expected: 15.5.5 fixes the admissible interval at [0, 86400) under LEAP-SECOND OFF, so BOTH bounds shall be enforced - a negative argument-3 and 86400 exactly shall each set EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION - while 86399 stays legal; and a floating-point argument-3 shall keep its fractional seconds regardless of float width.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfoa.cob (argument-3 = 90000) aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): FORMATTED-DATETIME argument-3 is not in standard numeric time form: the value shall be >= 0 and < 86,400 (ISO §7.3.17 r5, LEAP-SECOND OFF - the only mode this compiler supports)', exit 1. VARIATION 1 (the FLOOR, never probed): rfg1.cob passes -1 through a PIC S9(7) item and aborts with the same diagnostic, exit 1. VARIATION 2 (the EXACT first illegal value, never probed - the prober bracketed 86399 and 90000 but not 86400 itself): rfg2.cob passes 86400 and aborts with the same diagnostic, exit 1. VARIATION 3 (a second float width): rfg3.cob renders 18867.8125 through a COMP-1 item, a COMP-2 item and a PIC 9(5)V9(6) item into format "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ssss" and gets C1=[19950215T0514278125], C2=[19950215T0514278125], FX=[19950215T0514278125] - all three identical, so the precision path is not COMP-2-specific.
rows.derivation: 15.40.3 r4 read at line 31408 plus 15.5.5 at line 29840: 'the value shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400.' I validated the OFF-mode premise the diagnostic cites by reading 7.3.17 GR1 and GR5 verbatim (lines 3999 and 4018); GR5 is 'When OFF is specified or implied, a standard numeric time form value shall be greater than or equal to zero and less than 86,400', so the diagnostic's citation is exact. The interval is half-open on both sides, which makes -1 and 86400 the two first-illegal values; a guard written as 'reject large values' would pass the prober's 90000 probe and fail both of mine. 15.3 rule 14 makes EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION the required consequence. 18867 s = 05:14:27 and .8125 at width 4 = 8125.
rows.probe: rfoa.cob (90000, checking ON); rfg1.cob (-1 via PIC S9(7), checking ON); rfg2.cob (86400 exactly, checking ON); rfg3.cob (COMP-1 vs COMP-2 vs PIC 9(5)V9(6), one program). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: FLOOR AXIS - 15.5.5 has a lower bound too and no probe on record had tested it; -1 aborts correctly.

EXACT-BOUNDARY AXIS - 86400 is the first illegal value and the prober's bracket (86399 legal, 90000 illegal) left a 3,601-value gap in which an off-by-one guard could hide. 86400 aborts, so the comparison is strict-less-than as 15.5.5 requires.

FLOAT-WIDTH AXIS - the note's precision defect was that the string channel never consulted the float representation. Agreement across COMP-1 (binary32), COMP-2 (binary64) and fixed-point in ONE program shows the channel reads the value rather than a single widened cast.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md (landed) for the Real-blind precision half; kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) for the range guard - CobolDate.SecondsOutOfStandardForm, re-verified at both interval endpoints; kb/Work/PB23.md for the neighbouring CLR-exception-to-EC conversion.

rows.expected: |argument-4| > 1439 shall set EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION however the argument is written - literal, data item or arithmetic expression - and setting the condition means aborting when checking is on and returning the implementor-defined result when it is off; 1439 shall stay legal.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo9.cob (argument-4 = 2000 as a literal, checking ON) aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): FORMATTED-DATETIME argument-4 is 2000 minutes; the magnitude shall be <= 1439, one minute less than a day (ISO §15.40.3 r5)', exit 1. VARIATION 1 (ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION argument-4, never probed): rfh1.cob passes OA + OB where OA = 1400 and OB = 40, and aborts naming '1440 minutes' - so the guard is reached through the expression path the note said the fix had to survive, not only through a literal or a plain data item. VARIATION 2 (checking OFF, never probed): rfh2.cob runs argument-4 = 2000 and then -9999 with checking off and prints OFFCHK=[spaces], OFFNEG=[spaces], REACHED-END, exit 0 - the implementor-defined result (A.1 item 90), with no three-character offset subfield and no widened returned value, which is the failure mode the note recorded for 9999. VARIATION 3 (legal magnitudes at non-hour multiples): rfm1.cob renders +0545 / -0545 / +05:45 / -05:45 for +-345 and +2359 for 1439.
rows.derivation: 15.40.3 r5 read at line 31410: 'Argument-4 is an integer specifying the offset from UTC expressed in minutes. If argument-4 is specified, the magnitude of the value shall be less than or equal to 1439.' Its NOTE (line 31408 in the printed order) fixes the reading: 'The offset value 1439 represents 23 hours 59 minutes, which is one minute less than a day.' 1439 is therefore the last legal magnitude and 1440 the first illegal one, and 15.3 rule 14 requires the exception condition beyond it. Because r5 constrains a VALUE and argument-4 may be an expression, the guard must be a runtime one on the evaluated operand - so an expression argument is the shape that distinguishes a real guard from a literal-folding check, and it is the shape no probe had run.
rows.probe: rfo9.cob (literal 2000, checking ON); rfh1.cob (OA + OB = 1440, checking ON); rfh2.cob (2000 and -9999, checking OFF); rfm1.cob (+-345, 1439, -1439 across both offset subformats). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: EXPRESSION-OPERAND AXIS - the prober used a literal and a data item. An arithmetic expression also reaches the guard and the diagnostic reports the EVALUATED value 1440, so the check is on the operand's value at run time.

CHECKING-OFF DISPOSITION - 15.3 rule 14 has two halves and only the abort had been measured. With checking off, 2000 and -9999 both yield the implementor-defined empty result and the run continues; in particular -9999 does not render a 166-hour, three-character offset subfield, which was the original note's concrete symptom.
LEGAL NON-HOUR-MULTIPLE MAGNITUDES - +-345 renders +0545 / -0545 correctly, so the guard did not come at the cost of the ordinary 60-minute split.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB11.md (status: landed) - CobolDate.OffsetOutOfRange; re-verified on the expression path and on the checking-off disposition.

rows.expected: Argument-4 shall be rejected whenever the time portion of argument-1 is neither a UTC format nor an offset format - in every spelling of a local time portion, basic and extended, with and without a fractional-seconds subfield - and shall be permitted over the UTC and offset formats.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo7.cob's FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmss" 153569 45296 120) draws 'error COBOLNET1633: ... its format 'YYYYMMDDThhmmss' has a LOCAL time portion - neither a UTC format (a trailing 'Z') nor an offset format (an explicit '+hhmm' / '+hh:mm' subformat), ISO §15.3.3.4-§15.3.3.6. §15.40.3 r6 bars the argument there', exit 70. VARIATION 1 (spellings of a local time portion, never probed): rfi1.cob draws the same COBOLNET1633 for the EXTENDED local format "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss", for the basic local format WITH a fraction "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss", and for the extended local format with a fraction "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.ss" - three diagnostics, exit 70. VARIATION 2 (the recogniser is real, not a Z-or-plus substring test): rfi2.cob rejects the mixed-form combined formats "YYYYMMDDThh:mm:ss", "YYYY-MM-DDThhmmss" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss+hh:mm" with COBOLNET1631 whose text cites 15.3.1.1/15.3.2/15.3.4 and adds 'note that basic and extended forms never mix'; rfp2.cob additionally rejects "YYYYMMDDThhmmss+hhmmhh" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ+hhmm". VARIATION 3 (the permitted complement): rfj1.cob and rfj2.cob specify argument-4 = 0 over the basic UTC, extended UTC, basic offset, extended offset and fraction-bearing UTC formats and all are accepted and render correctly.
rows.derivation: 15.40.3 r6 read at line 31412: 'Argument-4 shall not be specified if the time portion of the format in argument-1 is neither a UTC format nor an offset format.' 15.3.3.4 (line 29695) says local formats 'contain only that information which is common to all time formats'; 15.3.3.5 (line 29700) says a UTC format is a common time format 'followed by a single uppercase Z character'; 15.3.3.6 says an offset format is a common time format followed by an offset subformat. A fractional-seconds subfield is part of the COMMON time format per 15.3.3.2, so "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss" is still LOCAL and argument-4 is still barred - a predicate that keyed on the presence of a '.' or on the format's length would have passed the prober's single basic probe and failed this one. 15.3.3.7 (line 29750) supplies the independent check: 'Combinations of basic date formats with extended time formats, or of extended date formats with basic time formats, are not allowed', so the mixed forms must be refused at r2 and that refusal is the evidence a real 15.3.1/15.3.2 recogniser exists rather than the substring proxy the note warned about.
rows.probe: rfo7.cob (the note's original local format with argument-4); rfi1.cob (extended local, basic-with-fraction, extended-with-fraction, each with argument-4); rfi2.cob and rfp2.cob (mixed and malformed formats); rfj1.cob / rfj2.cob (argument-4 over UTC and offset formats, accepted). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: LOCAL-FORMAT SPELLING AXIS - three further spellings of 'the time portion is local' all draw COBOLNET1633, including the two carrying a fractional-seconds subfield, so the predicate is on the time portion's KIND and not on its shape or length.

RECOGNISER-QUALITY AXIS - the 15.3.3.7 basic/extended mixing prohibition is enforced, and so are a trailing 'hh' run after an offset subformat and a 'Z' followed by an offset subformat. A 'Z or + anywhere' proxy would accept all of those; a real recogniser rejects them, which is what the note said this rule's fix required.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB11.md (status: landed) - the format-recogniser landing carrying COBOLNET1633 and COBOLNET1631; re-verified against the substring-proxy hypothesis the note named.

rows.expected: With the time portion a UTC or offset format and argument-4 omitted, the function shall return exactly what it returns for an explicit argument-4 of 0 - in every spelling of those two format kinds, basic and extended, with and without a fractional-seconds subfield; and an omitted argument-4 over an offset format shall render +0000 / +00:00.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfj2.cob prints UTC-OMIT=[20210616T123456Z] and UTC-ZERO=[20210616T123456Z] -> UTC=SAME; OFF-OMIT=[20210616T123456+0000] and OFF-ZERO=[20210616T123456+0000] -> OFF=SAME. VARIATION 1 (EXTENDED spellings, never probed): rfj1.cob prints EXTZ-OMIT=[1995-02-15T12:34:56Z] = EXTZ-ZERO -> EXTZ=SAME, and EXTO-OMIT=[1995-02-15T12:34:56+00:00] = EXTO-ZERO -> EXTO=SAME. VARIATION 2 (fraction-bearing UTC format, never probed): rfj1.cob prints FRZ-OMIT=[19950215T12345600Z] = FRZ-ZERO -> FRZ=SAME. VARIATION 3 (both branches of r7's premise are genuinely distinct paths): the same programs show the UTC branch producing a Z and the offset branch producing +0000/+00:00, so the equality is measured on two different renderings rather than on one shared one.
rows.derivation: 15.40.3 r7 read at line 31414: 'If argument-4 is omitted and the time portion of the format in argument-1 is a UTC format or an offset format, the function shall be evaluated as though 0 were specified for argument-4.' 'As though 0 were specified' is unconditional and admits no observable difference, so equality of the two spellings IS the rule and it must hold for every format its premise admits - four spellings, since 15.3.3.5 and 15.3.3.6 each have a basic and an extended form, and 15.3.3.2 adds the fractional variant of each. The prober tested one basic UTC and one basic offset format; the extended and fraction-bearing spellings take different tokenizer paths (the colons and the decimal separator are in-data characters per 15.3.3.1 and 15.3.3.2) and are exactly where a normalization block skipped for the omitted spelling could still differ. 15.3.3.6.1's receiving-field rule independently fixes the offset branch's expected value: 'If the values contained in offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields ... are both zero, the position corresponding to the plus sign in the format shall contain a plus sign', with NOTE 3 giving +0000 basic and +00:00 extended - both of which are what the omitted spelling prints.
rows.probe: rfj2.cob (basic UTC and basic offset, omitted vs explicit 0, compared with IF in-program); rfj1.cob (extended UTC, extended offset and fraction-bearing basic UTC, same comparison). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: EXTENDED-SPELLING AXIS - both extended forms give identical results for the two spellings, and the extended offset form independently produces 15.3.3.6.1 NOTE 3's +00:00.
FRACTIONAL-SUBFIELD AXIS - a UTC format with a fractional-seconds subfield also gives identical results, so the fraction rendering is not a place where the omitted and explicit-0 paths diverge.

rows.expected: (a) ACCEPT half: a constant-name standing for an alphanumeric/national literal IS the literal r1 requires, so `01 TFMT CONSTANT AS "hh:mm:ss".` + FORMATTED-TIME(TFMT, 45296) must give 12:34:56 with no diagnostic. (b) REJECT half: a literal of any OTHER class must draw a bind-time class diagnostic. I re-derived both and then attacked the CLASS AXIS THROUGH THE CONSTANT-NAME CHANNEL, which the prober never combined: if RefExpr's new substitution loses the literal's Category on the way in, a boolean or numeric constant-name would slip past the very screen the prober verified only on a directly-written B"0101".
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED, and the constant-name channel preserves Category. r1v1 `01 BFMT CONSTANT AS B"0101".` -> `error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME argument-1 is of class boolean; ISO 15.3 requires class alphanumeric, alphanumeric (numeric-edited) or national (15.41.3 r1/r3/r4)` + COBOLNET1631. r1v2 `01 NFMT CONSTANT AS 12345.` -> `COBOLNET1627 ... argument-1 is of class numeric` + COBOLNET1517. r1v3 `01 CFMT CONSTANT AS "hh" & ":mm:ss".` -> CATCONST=[12:34:56            ]. All three behave identically at --std 2014. The recorded COBOLNET0844 false rejection does not reproduce on any argument-1 form I could build.
rows.derivation: §15.41.3 1) (read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31451) 'Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal.' §13.10.4 GR1 makes constant-name-1 equivalent to literal-1 wherever it is written, unconditionally, so the accept half follows: rejecting TFMT rejects legal source. The reject half follows from r1's enumeration being exhaustive - boolean (§8.5.2.1) and numeric are neither of the two admitted classes - and the compiler's own precedent (COBOLNET1546 for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF) makes a §15 argument-class rule a bind-time diagnostic. A constant-name defined by an §8.8.3 concatenation is still an alphanumeric literal by §13.10.4 GR1, so r1v3 must be accepted.
rows.probe: r1v1.cob (RFT1311V1) boolean constant-name; r1v2.cob (RFT1311V2) numeric constant-name `01 NFMT CONSTANT AS 12345.`; r1v3.cob (RFT1311V3) concatenation-defined constant `01 CFMT CONSTANT AS "hh" & ":mm:ss".`, each `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(<c>, 45296) TO R.` Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run, and r1v1/r1v3 repeated at --std 2014. CONCATENATION-DEFINED CONSTANT (§8.8.3 inside the CONSTANT AS entry, an argument-1 spelling the prober never wrote): accepted and correct.
EDITION AXIS: the accept half and the reject half both hold at --std 2014, the lower edition in the row's window, which the prober ran only at 2023.

rows.expected: argument-2 must be a value in standard numeric time form: >= 0 and < 86,400 under LEAP-SECOND OFF. Out-of-range values must set EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal under checking ON, implementor-defined result otherwise). I attacked the axis the prober left fixed: they drove the range guard only through numeric LITERALS and DISPLAY-usage data items. If the guard sits in the fixed-point rendering arm only, an argument-2 arriving through the FLOATING-POINT leaf, through a BINARY leaf, or as the value of an ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION would bypass it - and RV-15.41.4-1's own history is that this function has separate Real and Dec arms.
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED on every channel. r3v1 (arithmetic expressions `A + A` = 90592 and `A - 90000` = -44704 from `01 A PIC 9(5) VALUE 45296.`) -> EXPR-OOR=[                    ] and EXPR-NEG=[                    ]. r3v2 (`01 FL USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 90000.5.` under "hhmmss.ss") -> FLT-OOR=[                    ]. r3v6 (`01 BD USAGE BINARY-DOUBLE VALUE 90000.`) -> BINDBL-OOR=[                    ]. Under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` the SAME two channels raise the exception, not merely a blank: r3v4 (FLOAT-LONG) and r3v5 (expression) both give `abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): FORMATTED-TIME argument-2 is not in standard numeric time form: the value shall be >= 0 and < 86,400 (ISO 7.3.17 r5, LEAP-SECOND OFF - the only mode this compiler supports)`. The recorded fabrication of hh=25 does not reproduce anywhere.
rows.derivation: §15.41.3 3) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31455) 'Argument-2 shall be a value in standard numeric time form.' §15.5.5 fixes that form as seconds past midnight, >= 0 and < 86,400 under the OFF phrase. §15.6's Table 21 row types argument-2 'Num2', i.e. §15.3 type 10 numeric - an arithmetic expression or a numeric data item - so a FLOAT-LONG item, a BINARY-DOUBLE item and an arithmetic expression are all legal argument-2 FORMS whose VALUE the range rule still governs. §15.3 sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION for an incorrect argument value and leaves the result implementor-defined only when checking is not enabled; a blank result under checking OFF plus a fatal EC under checking ON is exactly that disposition.
rows.probe: r3v1.cob (RFT1333V1) expression argument-2, both signs; r3v2.cob (RFT1333V2) FLOAT-LONG 90000.5; r3v6.cob (RFT1333V6) BINARY-DOUBLE 90000; r3v4.cob (RFT1333V4) and r3v5.cob (RFT1333V5) repeat the float and expression cases under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`. Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run. Outputs verbatim in 'actual'.
variations: FLOATING-POINT CHANNEL: a FLOAT-LONG argument-2 out of range is guarded, so the guard is not confined to the fixed-point rendering arm - the two-arm risk this function historically carried (Real vs Dec) does not apply to the range screen.
ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSION CHANNEL, in both directions (over 86,400 and negative): guarded, so the screen is on the computed value and not on a foldable literal.
BINARY-DOUBLE (native binary leaf) argument-2: guarded.

CHECKING-ON x NON-LITERAL: the prober showed the fatal EC only for a literal argument-2; I confirmed the exception is genuinely SET (not merely a blank result) on the float and expression channels too, which is the half §15.3 actually mandates.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) for the range guard; kb/Work/PB1.md / PB12.md (landed) for the class screen. The prober's attribution stands.

rows.expected: r4 has TWO halves and the prober claimed both enforced. MAGNITUDE: |argument-3| <= 1439. INTEGER-NESS: argument-3 is 'an integer representation', typed Int3 in §15.6's Table 21, so §15.3 type 6 governs it - and §5.5 2) resolves what 'integer' constrains an operand to be: a) a LITERAL argument-3 shall be an INTEGER LITERAL per §8.3.3.3.2; b) a data-name argument-3 shall reference an integer intrinsic function or a FIXED-POINT numeric data item with no digit positions right of the radix point. Therefore `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm", 45296, 120.75)` and a `USAGE FLOAT-LONG` argument-3 are BOTH non-conforming source and must be diagnosed exactly as the compiler already diagnoses `PIC S9(4)V99`.
rows.actual: ⛔ THE INTEGER-NESS HALF IS NOT ENFORCED - it is enforced on exactly ONE of the three operand shapes §5.5 2) covers, which is the two-arm-dispatch shape this project has hit five times. r4v3: `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm", 45296, 120.75) TO R.` compiles CLEAN and prints A3LIT=[123456+0200         ] - the fractional literal is silently truncated toward zero, no diagnostic, at --std 2023 AND --std 2014. r4v2: `01 FO USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 120.75.` -> A3FLOAT=[123456+0200         ], clean. r4v6: `01 FW USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 120.` -> A3FLTWHOLE=[123456+0200] and `01 FS USAGE FLOAT-SHORT VALUE 120.5.` -> A3FLTSHORT=[123456+0200], both clean - so a floating-point argument-3 is unscreened regardless of its VALUE, which is the stricter §5.5 2) b) 2 violation (a float item is not a fixed-point data item at all). r4v5: a NEGATIVE fractional literal `-120.9` -> A3NEGFRAC=[12:34:56-02:00      ], clean. THE ASYMMETRY IS IN THE SAME BUILD, not a regression: r4ctl.cob re-runs the prober's own control `01 F3 PIC S9(4)V99 VALUE 120.75.` and it still draws `error COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME argument-3 is a numeric data item with digits to the right of the decimal point, which ISO 15.3 type 6 does not admit - it requires an integer data item or an always-integral arithmetic expression (15.41.3 r1/r3/r4)`. The compiler states the rule in its own diagnostic text and then applies it to one operand shape out of three. (The MAGNITUDE half does hold everywhere I attacked it: r4v1 expression `K + K` = 2000 -> blank; r4v4 FLOAT-LONG 2000.5 -> blank and the literal boundary 1440 -> blank; so that half is genuinely landed and is not what overturns the row.)
rows.derivation: §15.41.3 4) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31457) 'Argument-3 is an integer representation of offset from UTC expressed in minutes. If argument-3 is specified, the magnitude of the value shall be less than or equal to 1439.' §15.6's Table 21 (cite.py --find -> §15.6 4)) types the row 'Anum1 or Nat1, Num2, Int3', so argument-3 is §15.3 type 6: 'Integer. An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified.' (cite.py --check 15.3 -> OK, §15.3 6)). What 'integer' constrains an operand to be is not left open - §5.5 2) a) (cite.py --find -> §5.5 2) a), 'Integer operands'): 'if that operand is a literal, it shall be an integer literal, as defined in 8.3.3.3.2, Fixed-point numeric literals'; §5.5 2) b) 2 (cite.py --find -> §5.5 2) b) 2.): 'a fixed-point numeric data item, other than an intrinsic function, whose description does not include any digit positions to the right of the radix point'. 120.75 is not an integer literal; a USAGE FLOAT-LONG/FLOAT-SHORT item is not a fixed-point numeric data item. Both are therefore non-conforming argument-3 operands, and silently truncating them to 120 minutes returns an answer for a program the standard does not admit.
rows.probe: r4v3.cob (RFT1334V3): `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm", 45296, 120.75) TO R.` -> A3LIT=[123456+0200         ] (also at --std 2014).  r4v2.cob (RFT1334V2): `01 FO USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 120.75.` as argument-3 -> A3FLOAT=[123456+0200         ].  r4v6.cob (RFT1334V6): FLOAT-LONG 120 -> A3FLTWHOLE=[123456+0200], FLOAT-SHORT 120.5 -> A3FLTSHORT=[123456+0200].  r4v5.cob (RFT1334V5): literal -120.9 under "hh:mm:ss+hh:mm" -> A3NEGFRAC=[12:34:56-02:00      ].  r4ctl.cob (RFT1334CTL): the prober's `01 F3 PIC S9(4)V99 VALUE 120.75.` -> COBOLNET1627, same build, proving the asymmetry.  Magnitude controls r4v1.cob (`K + K` = 2000 -> blank) and r4v4.cob (FLOAT-LONG 2000.5 -> blank; literal 1440 -> blank).  Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run.
variations: OPERAND SHAPE of argument-3 - the axis the prober held fixed at a single scaled DISPLAY data item: literal, floating-point data item and fixed-point scaled data item are three shapes §5.5 2) covers and only the third is screened.
VALUE-INDEPENDENCE on the float arm: FLOAT-LONG 120 (whole) is accepted just as FLOAT-LONG 120.75 is, so the gap is a missing USAGE/shape test, not a value test that rounds.
SIGN: the negative fractional literal -120.9 truncates to -120 silently, so the gap is not sign-guarded.
EDITION: the literal arm is unscreened at --std 2014 as well as 2023, the whole window this rule covers.
SEPARATION FROM THE MAGNITUDE HALF: expression 2000, FLOAT-LONG 2000.5 and literal 1440 all take the EC path, so the magnitude guard is landed and the row is live on the integer-ness half alone.
rows.mechanism: Binder layer, PB12's per-position argument schema: the `'i'` (integer) kind for FORMATTED-TIME position 3 is tested only against a bound FIXED-POINT numeric data item's scale - the diagnostic's own wording, 'argument-3 is a numeric data item with digits to the right of the decimal point', names the only shape it inspects - so a BoundNumLiteral with a nonzero scale and a floating-point (Real) leaf both fall through the screen and are then narrowed to whole minutes by IntrinsicRenderer's ArgInt cast; the fix is to make the `'i'` predicate a test over §5.5 2)'s three operand shapes (integer literal / integer intrinsic function / fixed-point item with zero scale, and reject Real usages outright) rather than a scale probe on one node kind.
rows.attribution: n/a (STILL-LIVE). Partial credit: kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) closed the |argument-3| <= 1439 magnitude half completely - verified above on the expression, float and boundary axes - and kb/Work/PB12.md (landed) introduced the per-POSITION `'i'` kind that closes the fixed-point arm of the integer-ness half. PB12's own body records the FORMATTED-* rows as the motivating case for per-position kinds, so the residue is inside a landed note's scope rather than outside it.

rows.expected: argument-3 supplied with a LOCAL time format must be diagnosed at bind. The prober probed only DIRECTLY-WRITTEN alphanumeric format literals ('hh:mm:ss' and 'hhmmss'). The classifier has to read the format TEXT, so the axis that could break it is argument-1 written in a form whose text is not a plain BoundStringLiteral's Text: a CONSTANT-NAME, an §8.8.3 CONCATENATION, a NATIONAL literal, and the §8.3.3.2 Format-2 HEXADECIMAL alphanumeric literal. If the classifier falls back to 'unknown format => permit', every one of those becomes a silent re-opening of the recorded defect.
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED on all four argument-1 spellings. r5v1 `01 LFMT CONSTANT AS "hh:mm:ss".` + (LFMT, 45296, 120) -> `error COBOLNET1633: ... but its format 'hh:mm:ss' has a LOCAL time portion ... 15.41.3 r5 bars the argument there`. r5v2 ("hh" & "mmss", 45296, 120) -> COBOLNET1633 naming the RESOLVED text 'hhmmss'. r5v3 (N"hh:mm:ss", 45296, 120) -> COBOLNET1633. r5v4 (X"68686D6D7373", 45296, 120) -> COBOLNET1633 naming 'hhmmss'. In every case the diagnostic quotes the DECODED format text, so the classifier is reading through the literal form rather than pattern-matching source characters.
rows.derivation: §15.41.3 5) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31461; cite.py --check 15.41.3 -> OK, §15.41.3 5)) 'Argument-3 shall not be specified if the time portion of the format in argument-1 is neither a UTC format nor an offset format.' §15.3.3.4-15.3.3.6 make a format with no trailing 'Z' and no offset subformat a LOCAL format. r1 makes argument-1 a literal, and §13.10.4 GR1 (constant-name), §8.8.3 (concatenation), §8.3.3.5 (national) and §8.3.3.2 Format 2 (hexadecimal alphanumeric) are all literal forms whose VALUE is known at compile time - so §4.2.2 requires each of them to be flagged, not just the plainly-written one.
rows.probe: r5v1.cob (RFT1335V1) constant-name local format; r5v2.cob (RFT1335V2) concatenation "hh" & "mmss"; r5v3.cob (RFT1335V3) national N"hh:mm:ss"; r5v4.cob (RFT1335V4) hexadecimal X"68686D6D7373" - each `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(<fmt>, 45296, 120) TO R.` Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run. All four -> COBOLNET1633, text quoted in 'actual'.
variations: CONSTANT-NAME argument-1 (a form that only became bindable with R01, i.e. a channel that did not exist when the classifier was written): still classified, so the two landings compose.
CONCATENATION argument-1: the classifier reads the folded text, not the source spelling.
NATIONAL and HEXADECIMAL argument-1 literal forms: both classified, so the screen is on the decoded characters and not on an alphanumeric-only path.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB11.md (landed), COBOLNET1633. The prober's attribution stands.

rows.expected: Omitting argument-3 with a UTC or offset format must be indistinguishable from specifying 0, on every observable argument-2. The prober's pairs were all alphanumeric-format, and their out-of-range pair was checked only with EC checking OFF (where both arms return the same blank). The axes that could still separate the two paths: a NATIONAL format literal (a different function-type arm), a FRACTION-BEARING argument-2 arriving through the floating-point leaf, the EXTENDED offset subformat with a fraction, and - the one that matters most - the out-of-range pair with CHECKING ON, where a guard emitted on only one of the two paths would raise the EC on one arm and not the other.
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED; every pair agrees. r6v1: NAT-OMIT=[12:34:56Z] = NAT-ZERO=[12:34:56Z] (N"hh:mm:ssZ"); FLT-OMIT=[12345650Z] = FLT-ZERO=[12345650Z] (`01 FL USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 45296.5.` under "hhmmss.ssZ"); EXTOFF-OMIT=[12:34:56.50+00:00] = EXTOFF-ZERO=[12:34:56.50+00:00] ("hh:mm:ss.ss+hh:mm", fraction-bearing float). r6v2/r6v3: the recorded divergent pair ("hh:mm:ssZ", 90000) run under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` - BOTH the omitted form and the ,0 form abort with the identical `abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): FORMATTED-TIME argument-2 is not in standard numeric time form ...`, so the r3 guard is emitted on both paths and the equivalence survives the mode the prober did not test. The recorded 25:00:00Z fabrication does not reproduce.
rows.derivation: §15.41.3 6) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31463) 'If argument-3 is omitted and the time portion of the format in argument-1 is a UTC format or an offset format, the function shall be evaluated as though 0 were specified for argument-3.' An unqualified equivalence: any argument-2, any admitted format, any exception-checking mode on which the two forms differ is a violation. §15.3.3.6.1's receiving-field rule fixes the zero-magnitude offset rendering at a plus sign, which is what the +00:00 pairs show. §15.41.1's type table makes a national argument-1 yield a national result, so the national pair also exercises a distinct return arm.
rows.probe: r6v1.cob (RFT1336V1) runs three omit/zero pairs back to back: N"hh:mm:ssZ" at 45296; "hhmmss.ssZ" with `01 FL USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 45296.5.`; "hh:mm:ss.ss+hh:mm" with the same FL.  r6v2.cob (RFT1336V2) and r6v3.cob (RFT1336V3) are the note's divergent pair split into two programs, each headed `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, so the EC aborts can be observed separately.  Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run. Outputs verbatim in 'actual'.
variations: EXCEPTION-CHECKING MODE, the axis the prober held fixed at OFF: with checking ON the out-of-range pair raises the SAME fatal EC on both the omitted and the ,0 form - a guard present on only one path would have shown here and did not.
NATIONAL format literal (a different §15.41.1 function-type arm): the pair agrees.
FLOATING-POINT, FRACTION-BEARING argument-2 through both a UTC and an EXTENDED OFFSET format: the pairs agree, so the equivalence holds on the value channel R24 rebuilt, not only on the integer path.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/PB11.md (landed). The prober's attribution stands.

rows.expected: A FRACTION-PART argument outside class numeric shall be rejected, and the rejection must not depend on the statement the reference sits in nor on the reference FORM.
rows.actual: rf02a (RF02A, --std 2023, exit 70): THREE COBOLNET1627s, one per statement - 'FUNCTION FRACTION-PART argument-1 is of class alphanumeric; ISO 15.3 requires class numeric (15.42.3 r1)' from the DISPLAY channel, from the IF relation-condition channel, and from the 8.4.3.2.3 SR2 keyword-omitted reference under REPOSITORY FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.
rows.derivation: 15.42.3 1) read verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31495 - 'Argument-1 shall be of the class numeric.' (NOTE: the prober's derivation drops the word 'the'; `cite.py --check 15.42.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric."` FAILS for exactly that reason, while the sibling rows 15.44.3/15.49.3/15.60.3/15.61.3 do use the wording the prober quoted and --check OK. The rule is real and the prober's status is unaffected; the quote is not verbatim.) 8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts PIC X in class alphanumeric, so the argument is excluded.
rows.probe: rf02a.cob (RF02A): REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC. / 01 X4 PIC X(4) VALUE "1234" / DISPLAY FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(X4) / IF FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(X4) = 0 / COMPUTE R = FRACTION-PART(X4). cmd: cobol.exe rf02a.cob --std 2023 -o rf02a.dll --run
variations: STATEMENT-CONTEXT axis (prober used COMPUTE only): DISPLAY channel -> 1627

The rule is a CONDITIONAL on the arithmetic mode, so it is implemented only if the mode changes the outcome: the same FLOAT-BINARY-64 item must be rejected under STANDARD-DECIMAL and accepted under NATIVE. Because FLOAT-BINARY-* and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL are both COBOL-2014 additions, the pair must also discriminate at --std 2014, and the bar must not be defeated by the operand's reference SHAPE (a subscripted element still 'specifies' the usage in its data description entry).

The rule's antecedent needs BOTH halves to exist: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY in effect, and a §3.167 usage (float-decimal-16 / float-decimal-34) on argument-1. Neither half is constructible, so the rule's condition can never be evaluated.

(VCR row 93)' then 'error COBOLNET0806: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL', exit=70. 01 FD1 USAGE FLOAT-DECIMAL-16 -> 'error COBOLNET1564: data item FD1: USAGE FLOAT-DECIMAL-16 (ISO/IEC 60559:2020 decimal64, ISO §13.18.60.4 GR17) is a processor-dependent language element not supported by COBOL.NET (Annex A.3 item 19): .NET provides no IEEE 754 decimal64 type', exit=70. rows.derivation: §15.43.3 r3 read verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31543. Both non-supports are conformance-sanctioned rather than defects: Annex A.3 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY processor-dependent (and §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 makes the mode obsolete), and Annex A.3 item 19 covers the FLOAT-DECIMAL usages — so the correct verdict is that the rule is unimplemented and its antecedent unreachable, not that the compiler diverges.

rows.derivation: SS15.67.3 1) 'Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or an alphanumeric or national data item whose content has one of the following two formats', where the two formats are [space-string][+|-][space-string]{digit[.[digit]] | .digit}[space-string] (leading sign only) and [space-string]{digit...}[space-string][+|-|CR|DB][space-string] (trailing sign only), and the where-list defines 'space-string is a string of one or more space characters'. Two consequences follow mechanically: a leading sign and a trailing sign/CR/DB together are in NEITHER format, and the only ignorable character is the space (U+0020) -- TAB/LF/CR/VT/FF/NBSP are ordinary characters, so a string containing one is outside both formats. SS15.3 then sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION. The class half is the sentence's own subject: an argument that is neither an alphanumeric/national literal nor such a data item violates r1, and SS4.2.2 makes that compile-time diagnosable.

rows.derivation: SS15.67.3 2) 'Leading and trailing spaces in argument-1 are ignored. Embedded spaces in argument-1 are ignored only if they appear before the first digit.' The word 'spaces' is defined by r1's own where-list -- 'space-string is a string of one or more space characters' -- i.e. ONE character, the space of the computer's alphanumeric or national character set. rows.expected: Re-derived independently. 15.67.3 3) 'If native arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 31.' (cite.py --check 15.67.3 -> OK, rule 3). Native is the default mode, so: an argument-1 carrying 32 or more DIGIT characters -- counting leading zeros, counting fraction digits, whatever separators/sign/space characters surround them -- violates r3; 15.3 then says 'the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist' and 'If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference'. So: checking OFF -> any implementor-defined result (0 is admissible, a NEGATIVE value for a sign-free argument is not, because it is a value and not a documented failure result the recorded defect produced by an unchecked Int128 wrap); checking ON -> the condition must be raised. And 31 digits must still be VALUED, in every channel and every surrounding shape.
rows.actual: Every recorded symptom is gone and the cap holds on every axis I attacked. r17.cob (PRORIG1701, the note's exact shapes): NV-D39=0.000000, NV-D39-SIGN=NOTNEG, NV-D39-STORE=000000000000000000000000000000{ into PIC S9(29)V9(2) -- positive-overpunch zero where the note measured -303715884.105728 and a '--170141183460469231731687303715884.105728' double-minus rendering. r1.cob (PRFN0101): D31=1234567890123456789012345678901.000000 (exact), D32=0.000000, D39=0.000000. The cap counts DIGITS, not string length, and counts them everywhere they occur: LZ32 ('0'x30+'12', 32 digits, value 12) = ZERO while LZ31 = VALUED / LZ31V=12.000000; PT31 ('1234567890123456789012345678.901', 31 digits across the decimal point) = VALUED while PT32 = ZERO; CR32 (32 digits + trailing CR, the OTHER general format) = ZERO; SGN31 ('  -'+31 digits+'  ') = VALUED / SGN31V=-12.000000, so the sign, the point, the spaces and the CR letters are NOT miscounted as digits. Channel sweep: ITEM32 (PIC X(40) data item) = ZERO, ITEM31 = VALUED; NEST32 (FUNCTION MAX(FUNCTION NUMVAL(<32>) 0)) = ZERO, NEST31 = VALUED; EXPR32 (COMPUTE R = FUNCTION NUMVAL(<32>) + 0) = 0. rows.derivation: SS15.67.3 5) 'The character period in argument-1 represents the decimal separator. When the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause is specified, the character comma shall be used in argument-1 instead of the character period to represent the decimal separator' (cite.py --check OK). SS12.3.4 1) 'The entries explicitly or implicitly specified in the configuration section of a source unit that contains other source units apply to each directly or indirectly contained source unit' (--check OK), and SS12.3.3 forbids a contained program from having its own configuration section -- so the contained program is ENTITLED to the comma and cannot restate it. 'Instead of' is a substitution: with the clause in effect the period is no longer the separator.
rows.probe: p10.cob (PNVA1001 with SPECIAL-NAMES. DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA., containing PNVA1002 which has no configuration section): COMPUTE R = FUNCTION NUMVAL("123,45") and FUNCTION NUMVAL("123.45") in each. Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run
rows.mechanism: A SCOPING defect in the binder, outside SS15.67: DataBinder.Switches.cs#DecimalPointIsComma is a per-source-unit property set only where the clause is textually bound, so the contained unit's DataBinder never sees the containing unit's SPECIAL-NAMES; IntrinsicRenderer.CommaFlag then reads the emitting unit's false flag and NUMVAL is compiled in period mode inside the contained program.

rows.expected: Re-derived independently. 15.69.3 2) 'If native arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in the significand shall not exceed 31.' (cite.py --check 15.69.3 -> OK, rule 2). The bound is on the SIGNIFICAND, and 15.69.3 r1's where-list separates it from the exponent ('n is one, two, three, or four digits representing the exponent'), so up to four exponent digits must NOT count. A 32-digit significand violates r2; 15.3 then permits an implementor-defined result with checking off and requires the condition to be raised with checking on. The recorded defect: no cap at all, an UNCHECKED Int128 accumulate, so 39 nines wrapped and a strictly positive argument returned a NEGATIVE value (-170141183460469231731687303715.884105728, 'Q' overpunch), with a latent Int128.Abs(Int128.MinValue) OverflowException in the same path.
rows.actual: Both the wrap and the latent CLR fault are unreachable, and the cap counts the significand. r17.cob (PRORIG1701, the note's exact shapes): NVF-D39 = FUNCTION NUMVAL-F('9'x39) = 0.000000000 and, stored into PIC S9(29)V9(2), NVF-D39-STORE=000000000000000000000000000000{ -- POSITIVE overpunch zero, no exception, no CLR fault. r3.cob (PRNF0301): F31=VALUED, F32=ZERO; NEG31=VALUED, NEG32=ZERO (the boundary holds with a leading minus, which the prober never signed); LZ31=VALUED, LZ32=ZERO (leading zeros counted); ITEM32=ZERO (alphanumeric PIC X(40) data item, not just a literal or a national item); NEST31=VALUED, NEST32=ZERO (inside FUNCTION MAX); EXP31=VALUED, EXP32=ZERO; and the decisive significand-vs-string test EXP31-4D = FUNCTION NUMVAL-F('1.234567890123456789012345678901E+0002') = VALUED -- 31 significand digits plus a FOUR-DIGIT exponent, 35 digit characters in the string, ACCEPTED, so the count is over the significand exactly as r2 says. MOVE-EXP31=00000012345678I = 123.456789, the correct value. r7.cob (PRNF0701): TRZ31 ('1.' + 30 zeros, 31 significand digits) = VALUED, TRZ32 = ZERO -- trailing fraction zeros are counted, which they must be; SPC31 ('  + ' + 31 ones + ' ') = VALUED, SPC32 = ZERO, so the sign and the r5-ignorable spaces are not miscounted. r6.cob (PRCM0601, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA): CMF31D=VALUED, CMF32D=ZERO. r12.cob (PRCK1201, checking ON): CTRL=00000015000000{ then 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): NUMVAL-F: argument-1 has more than 31 digits (32 so far), which the arithmetic mode in effect does not permit (ISO 15.69.3 rules 2-3)'. Editions: r3.cob at --std 2002 and --std 2014 gives a byte-identical result set.
rows.derivation: r2 bounds a count over a SUB-STRING of argument-1, so the two ways to get it wrong are counting the exponent (over-rejection) and failing to count part of the significand (over-acceptance). The four-digit-exponent probe (EXP31-4D) is the one that separates 'counts the significand' from 'counts the string', and the trailing-zero probe (TRZ31/TRZ32) is the one that separates 'counts significant digits' from 'counts digits'; r2 says digits, so TRZ32 must be rejected even though its value is 1.

rows.derivation: 8.4.3.2.3 SR2: "If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the source element, the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier." SR2 places NO restriction on which operand slot the keyword-omitted form may be written in, and SR1 bars a function-identifier only from a RECEIVING operand. The INSPECT TALLYING comparand (`TALLYING ... FOR ALL {identifier|literal}`) and the CONVERTING operands are SENDING operands, so the bare form is legal there. 15.30.2 is the two-word format `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION` with no argument list, and 15.2 says the function "may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified"; the type is alphanumeric. A conforming compiler must therefore accept the bare form in the INSPECT comparand, and the row cannot close while it rejects legal source there. (I checked the CALL leg against the standard before charging it: 14.9.4.3 SR3 -- "Identifier-2 shall reference an address-identifier or a data item defined in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section" -- means a function-identifier is NOT admissible as a Format-1 CALL argument, so COBOLNET0899 is the CORRECT answer and the keyword-omitted form's compile-clean/run-time-throw is the defect, not the rejection.)

One rule -- 'a bare word naming a repository intrinsic IS a function-identifier' -- written down in more than one place instead of once in the reference resolver every operand slot shares.

rows.expected: under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` the keyword-omitted reference `EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` must be accepted in every SENDING operand slot, exactly as `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` is
rows.actual: `INSPECT WS-ND TALLYING WS-C FOR ALL EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N.` (rxr6) -> `error COBOLNET1639`, while `... FOR ALL FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N.` (rxr7) compiles and runs (`C=000`). The diagnostic is COBOLNET1639 "is not defined - no declaration in this source element gives the name", i.e. the bare word is never resolved against the REPOSITORY intrinsic set in that slot -- LEGAL COBOL-2002+ SOURCE REJECTED. A second, independent slot fails the same way at RUN TIME: `CALL "..." USING BY CONTENT EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N.` compiles CLEAN and dies with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: CALL USING BY CONTENT argument 'BYCONTENTEXCEPTION-LOCATION-N'`, where the FUNCTION-written twin is correctly REJECTED at compile time (COBOLNET0899) -- two arms of one dispatch disagreeing about the same program. The prober's own FIXED evidence for these rows named the INSPECT slot (k4insp.cob, `INSPECT EXCEPTION-STATUS TALLYING WS-N FOR ALL "-"`), but that puts the bare name in the INSPECTED-ITEM slot only; the COMPARAND slot of the very same statement still rejects it. That is the recorded half-fix pattern -- one call site of several.
rows.derivation: 8.4.3.2.3 SR2: "If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph of the source element, the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier." SR2 places NO restriction on which operand slot the keyword-omitted form may be written in, and SR1 bars a function-identifier only from a RECEIVING operand. The INSPECT TALLYING comparand (`TALLYING ... FOR ALL {identifier|literal}`) and the CONVERTING operands are SENDING operands, so the bare form is legal there. 15.31.2 is the two-word format `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` with no argument list, and 15.2 says the function "may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified"; the type is national. A conforming compiler must therefore accept the bare form in the INSPECT comparand, and the row cannot close while it rejects legal source there. (I checked the CALL leg against the standard before charging it: 14.9.4.3 SR3 -- "Identifier-2 shall reference an address-identifier or a data item defined in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section" -- means a function-identifier is NOT admissible as a Format-1 CALL argument, so COBOLNET0899 is the CORRECT answer and the keyword-omitted form's compile-clean/run-time-throw is the defect, not the rejection.)
