rows.expected: SS15.34.2's general format is `FUNCTION EXP ( argument-1 )` - exactly ONE argument. SS8.3.3.3.3 r2 makes the sign part of a floating-point literal, so `-1.5E3`, `-1.5E-3` and `+1.5E+3` are each ONE literal; any diagnostic counting two arguments is a false rejection of legal source, and the value must be the correctly signed one.
rows.actual: Every form compiles and evaluates correctly: `EXP-NEGEXP =00000000099850112D` = 0.998501124 = e^(-0.0015) for `FUNCTION EXP(-1.5E-3)`; the sibling `FUNCTION LOG10(+1.5E+3)` gives 3.176091259; the signed float literal also parses in a MULTI-argument function in both positions - `FUNCTION MAX(-1.5E3, 1)` = 1.000000000 and `FUNCTION MIN(1, -1.5E3)` = -1500.000000000 - and the non-intrinsic control `COMPUTE R = -1.5E3` gives the same -1500.000000000. Exit 0, no diagnostics.
rows.derivation: SS15.34.2 from lines 31168-31170: 'FUNCTION EXP ( argument-1 )' - one argument, no ellipsis. SS8.3.3.3.3 2) 'The literal to the left of the E represents the significand. It may be signed and shall include a decimal point' is the load-bearing rule: the sign belongs to the literal, so the token sequence is ONE argument. Expected values follow from SS15.34.4 r1 and SS15.56.4 r1.

rows.expected: The order and multiplicity of the format are normative. Ill-formed shapes the prober did not write: (i) ANYCASE REPEATED - `(H N ANYCASE ANYCASE)`, since a bracketed phrase is optional but not repeatable; (ii) LAST written AFTER argument-3 - `(H N START AFTER 1 LAST)`, since LAST precedes the argument-3 bracket in the written order; (iii) FOUR operand arguments - `(H N 1 2)`, since the format has at most three. All three owe a compile-time diagnostic. Well-formed shapes that must still answer over H="ABCABCABC", N="ABC" (occurrences 1, 4, 7): `(H N START AFTER SK ANYCASE)` with SK=1 -> 4; `(H N ANYCASE)` -> 1; `(H N SK)` -> 4.
rows.actual: All three ill-formed shapes are rejected at compile time, each naming what specifically went wrong. r18 -> `COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION FIND-STRING takes argument-1 argument-2 [LAST] [[START AFTER] argument-3] [ANYCASE], in that order (ISO 15.37.2) - ANYCASE is repeated`. r19 -> `- LAST follows a later phrase`. r20 -> `COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION FIND-STRING takes argument-1 argument-2 [[START AFTER] argument-3] (ISO 15.37.2); 4 operand argument(s) given`. The complement is intact rather than over-rejected: r21 -> OKSKIPANY=0004, OKANY=0001, OKBARE=0004, so a phrase word in a legal position still binds and the values are r1/r2's. Note that r20's arity message elides the [LAST] and [ANYCASE] phrases from the format it quotes while r18/r19 print them - a cosmetic inconsistency in one of two message builders, not a behaviour divergence.
rows.derivation: 15.37.2's general format, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md: `FUNCTION FIND-STRING argument-1 argument-2 [ LAST] [ [ START AFTER ] argument-3 ] [ ANYCASE ]`, with FUNCTION, FIND-STRING, LAST, START, AFTER and ANYCASE underlined. Underlined words are required as written where written; brackets make a phrase optional, and an optional phrase appears once at the position shown - so a second ANYCASE has no production and LAST after argument-3 is out of order. The operand count is bounded at three by the format, so a fourth operand has nowhere to land. Values for the legal forms follow from 15.37.4 r1 and r2 over the three occurrences of "ABC" in "ABCABCABC": plain 1, skip 1 gives 4, and ANYCASE changes nothing for an already-matching case.
rows.probe: r18.cob (RSL18) `MOVE FUNCTION FIND-STRING(H N ANYCASE ANYCASE) TO P.` / r19.cob (RSL19) `... (H N START AFTER 1 LAST) ...` / r20.cob (RSL20) `... (H N 1 2) ...`, each over `01 H PIC X(9) VALUE "ABCABCABC". 01 N PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC".` r21.cob (RSL21): the three legal forms plus `01 SK PIC 9(2) VALUE 1.` Command: cobol.exe r18.cob --std 2023 -o r18.dll --run -> exit 70.

LAST written after argument-3, a different out-of-order position from the prober's LAST-after-ANYCASE and LAST-before-the-operands
FOUR operand arguments, i.e. the arity bound rather than the phrase order
argument-3 supplied as a DATA ITEM under START AFTER together with ANYCASE, as a live complement control

rows.derivation: 15.38.2 read at line 31314: '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE</u> ( argument-1 )'. Both words underlined, therefore required per 5.2.3; the parenthesised part carries no brackets, so - unlike 15.75.2 RANDOM, whose parenthesised part IS bracketed - there is no bare form and no zero-argument form. 8.4.3.2.3 SR2's 'otherwise the word FUNCTION is required' governs absent a REPOSITORY declaration. The bare no-parenthesis spelling is the sharper test of the unbracketed-parentheses reading than '()' is, because a grammar that made the whole parenthesised part optional would accept the bare name silently.

rows.derivation: §15.41.2 General format (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31446) `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME ( argument-1 argument-2 [ argument-3 ] )`, both words underlined. §8.3.3.5.2 Format 2 gives the national literal's hexadecimal form with EITHER delimiter (NX"..." or NX'...'), and COBOL words are not case-sensitive, so nx and NX are the same word - each spelling is one national literal and §15.41.3 r1 admits it. The hex 0068/006D/0073 are 'h'/'m'/'s' and 002B is '+', so the formats are 'hhmmss' and 'hhmmss+hhmm'; 45296 = 12:34:56 renders 123456, and with a +120 offset the offset subfield is +0200. The general format's function-identifier admits reference modification of an alphanumeric/national result, so (1:5) of '12:34:56' is '12:34'.

The consequence: with that REPOSITORY entry and '01 TBL. 05 LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC PIC S999 OCCURS 3 TIMES.', 'MOVE 7 TO LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(2)' then 'MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1' with A1=2 prints SHADOW=+00000007.000 with ZERO diagnostics — the SR2 function reference of this format silently became the data item, returning 7 where -999 is required. ONE LEG IS FIXED: with no REPOSITORY at all, 'MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1' is now a proper compile-time rejection, 'error COBOLNET1543: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC is written without the word FUNCTION, but the REPOSITORY paragraph does not declare it. ISO §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 allows the omission only for an intrinsic named in REPOSITORY', exit=70 — the recorded unhandled run-time NotImplementedCobolFeatureException is gone. Conforming legs still hold: the SR2 form works under a REPOSITORY entry (KWOMIT-L=-00000999.000) and the name IS available as a user-defined word when no function-specifier names it (UDW=01K, correct per §8.3.2.1 r5's default).
rows.derivation: §15.58.2 read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:32156-32158. §8.3.2.1 rule 5's prohibition is the standard's own disambiguation mechanism for the SR2 alternative of this format; COBOL.NET substitutes a hand-written precedence policy ('a declared data item wins — never a mis-routed subscript'), which is sound ONLY if the illegal declaration is rejected. Because it is not, a conforming program written in this general format's SR2 alternative can silently return a different value.

rows.mechanism: DataBinder#Bind populates RepositoryIntrinsics / RepositoryAllIntrinsic, and those sets have consumers only at REFERENCE sites (IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction); there is no DECLARATION-time consumer anywhere, so §8.3.2.1 r5 is written down in no layer and the binder's data-item-wins tie-break silently re-points the reference. The defect is compiler-wide across every intrinsic-function-name — I confirmed it reproduces identically for HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC (p4302b HSHADOW=+00000007.000) — so it is one fix serving many inventory rows.

rows.expected: MOD's format is 'FUNCTION MOD ( argument-1 argument-2 )' - fixed at two, no braces, no ellipsis - so it does NOT permit an argument to be repeated a variable number of times and 15.3 r14 never grants it the ALL subscript. 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(E(ALL) B)' shall therefore be REJECTED at compile time regardless of how many occurrences E has.
rows.actual: Still accepted whenever the expansion happens to land on two arguments. p6422a (--std 2023 AND --std 85, identical): '05 E PIC S9(4) OCCURS 1 TIMES.' with E(1) = 7 and B = 3 compiles CLEAN - zero diagnostics - and prints 'ALL1 = 000A' (PIC S9(4) overpunch A = +1, i.e. MOD(7,3) = 1). p6422b, the identical program with 'OCCURS 3 TIMES': 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION MOD takes 2 argument(s); 4 given (ISO 15.3)' - note the count FOUR, which is the arity screen measuring the OUTPUT of an expansion that should never have run. So the restriction is enforced only by the accident of the OCCURS count, exactly as recorded, and the one-occurrence table walks straight through.
rows.derivation: 15.64.2 general format '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>MOD</u> ( argument-1 argument-2 )' - two named arguments, no repetition notation. 15.3 14) 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL.' (cite.py --check 15.3 on that sentence -> OK §15.3 14) (Arguments)). The grant is CONDITIONAL on variable repetition; MOD has none, so the device is unavailable to it and the correct screen is on the function's ARITY KIND, not on the expanded element count.

rows.expected: Re-derived independently. 15.69.2 general format: 'FUNCTION NUMVAL-F ( argument-1 )' -- one required argument, no optional leg, no keyword. 15.69.3 1) puts 'an alphanumeric or national literal or data item' in that position, and 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 extends 'literal' to the figurative constants. So the row closes only if: (i) exactly one argument is accepted and 0 or 2 are diagnosed AT COMPILE TIME; (ii) every shape that is an alphanumeric/national literal or data item is accepted in the argument-1 position and VALUED rather than aborted at run time; (iii) a keyword that the format does not carry is rejected; and (iv) the edition gate does not refuse the format in an edition that has it. The recorded PARTIAL rested on exactly two grounds: the figurative constants aborting the run unit, and an IntroducedIn=2014 catalog row that made --std 2002 reject the function.
rows.actual: Both recorded grounds are closed and three further format questions answer correctly. ARITY: r4b.cob (PRNF0402, 'FUNCTION NUMVAL-F ( )') -> 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION NUMVAL-F takes 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO 15.3)'; r4c.cob (PRNF0403, 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION NUMVAL-F' with no parentheses at all) -> the same COBOLNET1504, 0 given; r4d.cob (PRNF0404, two arguments) -> COBOLNET1504, 2 given. All three are COMPILE-time, exit non-zero, no code emitted. KEYWORD INJECTION (not in the format): r8.cob 'FUNCTION NUMVAL-F("1.5E+2" ANYCASE)' and r8b.cob 'FUNCTION NUMVAL-F(LOCALE "1.5E+2")' both fail to compile (COBOLNET1639 'ANYCASE'/'LOCALE' is not defined, plus COBOLNET1504 takes 1; 2 given) -- so NUMVAL-F does not inherit the positionally-blind keyword sweep that leaves FMT-15.68.2 still-live for NUMVAL-C. ARGUMENT-1 SHAPES, all -> 150.000000 (00000015000000{): r4.cob (PRNF0401) GROUP (a group item over '1.5'+'E+02'), NATREFMOD (reference modification NN(3:6) on PIC N(20)), NESTED (inside FUNCTION MAX); r10_hex.cob (a hexadecimal alphanumeric literal X'312E35452B32'), r10_natlit.cob (a bare national literal N"1.5E+2"), r10_concat.cob (a concatenation expression "1.5" & "E+2"), r10_tbl.cob (a SUBSCRIPTED table element TE(2)), r10_trimnest.cob (a nested string-valued intrinsic FUNCTION TRIM('  1.5E+2  ')). FIGURATIVES, the note's ground (a): r4e.cob (PRNF0405) NOKEYWORD=00000015000000{ (REPOSITORY form, FUNCTION keyword omitted), ZEROFIG=00000000000000{, ALLLIT=00000000100000{ (=1, the 8.3.3.6.4 GR3 c) one-occurrence image), SPACEFIG=00000000000000{, then REACHED-END -- no NotImplementedCobolFeature abort. EDITION GATE, the note's ground (b): r4.cob compiles AND RUNS identically at --std 2002, 2014 and 2023 (CTRL/GROUP/NATREFMOD/NESTED all 150), while --std 85 gives four x 'error COBOLNET1502: FUNCTION NUMVAL-F was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 (15) - it requires --std 2002 or later'. The 2002 window is carried by kb/Work/R28.md, a LANDED adjudication that states in terms that the 2023 text cannot supply the window and sources it externally -- so it is a decided item, not an inherited guess.
rows.derivation: A general format is closed in three directions, and the prober tested two of them. Arity in the excess direction (2 args) they tested; arity in the DEFICIT direction (0 args, and the no-parentheses spelling) they did not, and that is where a binder that computes arity from a surviving operand list typically leaks -- it is exactly how FMT-15.68.2 fails for NUMVAL-C. Keyword injection is the third direction: the format carries no keyword, so ANYCASE/LOCALE must be refused. And 15.69.3 r1 plus 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 name a SET of admissible argument-1 shapes, so the accept direction is only closed by probing shapes the prober did not: hex literal, bare national literal, concatenation expression, subscripted table element.

AXIS THE PROBER DID NOT VARY #2 -- KEYWORD INJECTION. ANYCASE and LOCALE, the two keywords the sibling NUMVAL-C format carries and whose handling leaves FMT-15.68.2 still-live, are both rejected here.

AXIS THE PROBER DID NOT VARY #3 -- four further argument-1 shapes admitted by 15.69.3 r1: a HEXADECIMAL alphanumeric literal, a bare NATIONAL LITERAL (they used a national data item), a CONCATENATION expression "1.5" & "E+2", and a SUBSCRIPTED TABLE ELEMENT. All four value to 150.000000.

rows.expected: r3 requires the returned byte count to INCLUDE the implicit filler positions, and 8.5.1.6.3 fixes which filler must exist (not implementor-defined outside the SYNCHRONIZED bullet). On axes the prober did not vary: (i) a bit item one level DEEPER - `01 NG1. 05 SUBG. 10 NB PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT. 10 NA PIC X.` -> NB takes bit 0 of byte 0, 5 filler bits advance NA to its byte boundary, so SUBG = 2 and NG1 = 2; (ii) THREE adjacent bit siblings 3+3+3 - `01 TB.` -> 9 bits, then end-of-record filler to an integral number of characters = 16 bits = 2 bytes (a per-item-rounding model would give 3, a no-packing model 3); (iii) an EXACTLY-INTEGRAL group 4+4 bits - `01 EB.` -> 8 bits = 1 byte with NO filler at all, the negative side of the rule; (iv) a bit item followed by a non-DISPLAY item - `01 BC. 05 BC1 PIC 1(3) BIT. 05 BC2 PIC 9(4) COMP.` -> 1 + 2 = 3; (v) a LEVEL 77 bit item, which 8.5.1.6.3's NOTE explicitly EXCLUDES from end filler - `77 SVB PIC 1(5) USAGE BIT.` -> no filler, 5 bits, and r4 rounds to 1.
rows.actual: Every one lands on the derived value. r01 -> NG1BL=2, NG1LN=2, SUBGBL=2, TBBL=2, TBLN=2, EBBL=1, EBLN=1, BCBL=3, BCLN=3, SVBBL=1, SVBLN=5. The integral case (EB=1) and the no-filler level-77 case (SVB) are the two that separate a real 8.5.1.6.3 layout from a blanket ceiling, and both are right. RESIDUAL FOUND HERE, NOT AN OVERTURN OF THIS ROW: the rule cannot be exercised on a TABLE of bit items at all - `01 BTG. 05 BTE OCCURS 3 TIMES PIC 1(3) USAGE BIT.` (r02) fails in the BACKEND with `error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'string[]' to 'string'` / `error CS0029`, and again with a fixed prefix (r27, `05 BX PIC X(2). 05 BTE OCCURS 2 TIMES PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT.`). The same table without USAGE BIT compiles and answers (r02b -> BTDBL=9), so OCCURS+USAGE BIT is the trigger. That is a new defect on a different axis (codegen), logged in refute-summary; r3's recorded defect - filler being VACUOUS because nothing was ever sub-byte - is genuinely gone.
rows.derivation: 15.14.4 r3 (cite.py --check OK): "The returned value shall include the number of implicit filler positions, if any, in argument-1." What must exist is 8.5.1.6.3 (cite.py --check OK): filler is generated "Following a bit data item within an alphanumeric group item ... as needed to advance alignment to a required natural boundary for the next item within that group" and following a trailing bit data item "as needed to increase the number of bits to fill an integral number of characters"; adjacent elementary bit items of the same level align "at the next bit position in storage" (which is why TB is 9 packed bits, not 3 separate bytes); and the NOTE withholds end filler from "a level 77 item, or ... a level 1 elementary item". Only the SYNCHRONIZED bullet is "As defined by the implementor", so the non-SYNC filler above is owed, not optional.

rows.expected: r4 rounds a non-integral byte occupancy UP. Axes the prober did not vary: (i) a LEVEL 77 bit item, which 8.5.1.6.3's NOTE exempts from end filler so its occupancy is genuinely fractional (5/8 byte) rather than filler-completed - `77 SVB PIC 1(5) USAGE BIT.` -> 1; (ii) a bit item whose ROUNDING IS NOT NEEDED because the group is exactly integral - `01 EB. 05 E1 PIC 1(4) BIT. 05 E2 PIC 1(4) BIT.` -> 1 (8 bits, no rounding), which separates 'rounds up' from 'always adds a byte'; (iii) a bit item packed against a NON-DISPLAY neighbour - `01 BC. 05 BC1 PIC 1(3) BIT. 05 BC2 PIC 9(4) COMP.` -> 3; (iv) the LENGTH twin on the same items, which must NOT round because 15.50.4 r1 answers in boolean positions - SVB -> 5.
rows.actual: r01 -> SVBBL=1 with SVBLN=5, EBBL=1, EBLN=1, BCBL=3, BCLN=3, plus the nested and three-sibling records at 2 and 2. Correct on every axis. The recorded defect (one byte per boolean position, so r4's rounding was unreachable and the answer was n) does not reproduce anywhere. The EB=1 case is the one that matters most for this row: an implementation that satisfied the prober's 1/5/8/9/16/17 ladder by ceiling every bit item independently would still be right there, but it would give TB (3+3+3) 3 rather than 2 - and TB is 2, so the width really is computed over the packed layout and then rounded once.
rows.derivation: 15.14.4 r4 (cite.py --check OK): "When argument-1 does not occupy an integral number of bytes, the returned value is rounded to the next larger integer value." That an explicitly-USAGE-BIT item occupies BITS is 13.18.60.4 GR5 ("The USAGE BIT clause specifies that bits shall be used to represent a boolean data item") plus 8.5.1.6.3; the NOTE's exemption for a level-77 item is what makes SVB a genuine fractional-occupancy case rather than a filler-completed one. The complement is 15.50.4 r1, which answers an elementary boolean item in BOOLEAN positions - so LENGTH(SVB) must stay 5 while BYTE-LENGTH(SVB) becomes 1, and a fix that merely redefined the item's width would move both.

rows.actual: Still staged loud by name. ZSL07 -> `LN-DL=5` from FUNCTION LENGTH, then, on the very next statement, `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of a DYNAMIC LENGTH item (current length in bytes at runtime, ISO 15.14.4 rule 5)`. The value is demonstrably one arm away: LENGTH already publishes 5 for the same item in the same program. The NATIONAL sub-case (ZSL07C, `01 DN PIC N DYNAMIC LENGTH.` + `MOVE N"ABC" TO DN`) throws the IDENTICAL BYTE-LENGTH message, so the 2-bytes-per-position doubling is not reached either.
rows.derivation: 15.14.4 rule 5, quoted: "If argument-1 is a dynamic-length elementary item, the current length of argument-1 in bytes is returned." With the pinned 1-byte-per-DISPLAY-position model, "HELLO" is 5 bytes; for the national item N"ABC" it is 6. The rule's NOTE - "Any prefixed fields or delimiter characters are not included in the current length" - is satisfied by construction for a bare .NET string carrier.

rows.expected: `01 VLG. 05 F1 PIC X(4). 05 DL PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.` holding "HELLO" -> r6 a) 4 + r6 b) 5 = 9 bytes.
rows.actual: Reproduces as a SILENT wrong constant with no diagnostic and no loud stage. r22 -> LNVLG=0009 (the LENGTH twin is right) and BLVLG=0004 (BYTE-LENGTH omits exactly the variable part). The two readings sit in the same program on the same record, so this is not a build or environment difference: the same item is 9 through one intrinsic and 4 through the other. The prober's STILL-LIVE is sound, and the divergence is the harmful kind - a wrong number, not a loud stage.
rows.derivation: 15.14.4 r6, quoted: "If argument-1 is a variable-length group and the PHYSICAL argument is not specified, the value returned is the sum of the following: a) the lengths of all subordinate non-variable-length data-items; b) the current lengths of all subordinate dynamic-length elementary items; c) the lengths of all subordinate dynamic-capacity tables based on their current capacity." 8.5.1.12.1 makes VLG the subject (one dynamic-length elementary subordinate). F1 contributes 4 under a); DL holding "HELLO" contributes 5 under b); 4 + 5 = 9. The LENGTH twin's r7 has the identical three-term structure and answers 9 on the same record, which is independent corroboration of the arithmetic.

DISPLAY "LNVLG=" R.` + `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(VLG). DISPLAY "BLVLG=" R.` Command: cobol.exe r22.cob --std 2023 -o r22.dll --run -> exit 0, output LNVLG=0009 / BLVLG=0004.

rows.expected: `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(G PHYSICAL)` shall compile; for `01 G. 05 A PIC X(5).` - physically located where defined - r7 makes it return the same value as without PHYSICAL, i.e. 5.
rows.actual: The PHYSICAL argument still cannot be written for BYTE-LENGTH, so r7 has no implementation to adjudicate. ZSL09 -> `error COBOLNET1639: 'PHYSICAL' is not defined ...` followed by `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)`. This is now a HALF-SWEEP, and that is new information: the LENGTH twin ACCEPTS it - ZSL09B `DISPLAY FUNCTION LENGTH(G PHYSICAL).` prints 5, and ZSL09C proves the word is a real keyword there, not swallowed, because `FUNCTION LENGTH(G PHYSIKAL)` draws `COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION LENGTH takes argument-1 [PHYSICAL] (ISO 15.50.2); 2 operand argument(s) given`. Rejection is at COMPILE time by name, never a silent wrong answer, so the row stays NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than DIVERGES.
rows.derivation: 15.14.2's general format (specs/ISO_COBOL.md) is `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )` with FUNCTION, BYTE-LENGTH and PHYSICAL underlined and PHYSICAL bracketed - an optional required-word phrase. 15.14.4 rule 7, quoted: "If argument-1 is a variable-length group and the PHYSICAL argument is specified, the returned value is the length of argument-1 in number of bytes. If argument-1 is not physically located where it is defined, the returned value includes only the length of the implementor-defined pointer. If argument-1 is physically located where it is defined, BYTE-LENGTH returns the same value same value that would be returned had the PHYSICAL argument not been specified." (The duplicated 'same value' is in the printed standard; the 15.50.4 r8 twin does not have it.)

rows.expected: Re-derived from the rule text read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30373 -- 15.16.4 r2: 'If more than one character has the same position in the national program collating sequence, the character returned is the first character defined for that character position. If the order of multiple characters having the same position is undefined, the implementor shall define which of those multiple characters is returned; for a given implementation, collating sequence, and ordinal position, every invocation of the CHAR-NATIONAL function shall return the same character.' HALF 1 (behaviour): 12.3.7.4 GR7 1.6 defines the order for an ALSO phrase ('Literal-1 is the first character in the sequence of multiple characters defined at that ordinal position'), so the returned character shall be literal-1 -- irrespective of its code value, of where in the alphabet the ALSO group sits, of how many members it has, and of whether the operands are literals or ordinal numbers -- and every invocation shall agree. HALF 2 (the half the record left OPEN): Annex A.1 item 22 makes the determination a REQUIRED, DOCUMENTED implementor item, so docs/CONFORMANCE.md must carry the register row.
rows.actual: HALF 1 holds on three shapes the prober did not try. rfb1 (ALPHABET NAT-A FOR NATIONAL IS N"C" ALSO N"A" ALSO N"B", N"M" -- a THREE-member group whose literal-1 is the HIGHEST-coded member) -> T3-CN1=[C], T3-CN2=[M]. rfb2 (ALSO group at a NON-FIRST position: N"Z", N"C" ALSO N"A" ALSO N"B", N"M") -> MID-CN1=[Z], MID-CN2=[C], MID-CN3=[M], and a PERFORM loop over a DATA-ITEM ordinal gives INVAR01=[C] INVAR02=[C] INVAR03=[C] (the invocation-invariance sentence). rfb3 (the NUMERIC-ORDINAL alphabet operand form, a different binder path: ALPHABET NAT-C FOR NATIONAL IS 68 ALSO 66 ALSO 67, 78) -> ORDFORM-CN1=[C], ORDFORM-CN2=[M] -- ordinal 68 is code unit 67 = 'C', so literal-1 wins there too. HALF 2 is genuinely closed: docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries '| 22 | **CHAR-NATIONAL function - which one of the multiple characters is returned**, S15.16.4, required + documented | ... CHAR-NATIONAL returns **the FIRST character defined for that position** - deterministic, in the alphabet definition's own written order (CobolIntrinsics.CharNational over the emitted __COLLATE_NAT table; NationalCollation.CharAt is the one position->character reader, so the choice cannot vary by call site). |' -- read verbatim, and the documented determination MATCHES the measured behaviour rather than merely existing.

rows.derivation: 15.17.4 r1 (read at line 30403): 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows: argument-1 + (argument-2 / 100000)'. 143951 + 18867.812479168304/100000 = 143951.18867812479168304, which at scale 13 is .1886781247916 - what the COMPUTE arm and the spelled-out expression both produce, so the MOVE arm's .1886781247900 is the divergent one. 15.4.1's standard-arithmetic paragraph requires the returned value to equal that expression and to be 'the same for all instances of a given function within a single execution of the runtime element'; COMBINED-DATETIME is not among the four excepted functions. The refutation risk here was that the split might be an artifact of the receiver rather than of the function - excluded because EAE13, computed from the spelled-out expression into the SAME PIC 9(9)V9(13) item, carries all 13 digits.

rows.expected: Re-derived from the rule text read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md (15.18.4 r2): 'If argument-1 is of class or usage national, the function will return a national value.' The condition is on ARGUMENT-1 ALONE -- not on all arguments -- so: (i) a national argument-1 makes the result national however argument-2 is described and however argument-1 is written (data item OR literal), and 14.9.25.3 SR10 Table 16 (National sender x Alphabetic/Alphanumeric/Alphanumeric-edited receiver = 'No') then forbids the MOVE; (ii) a non-national argument-1 with a national argument-2 must NOT be promoted -- r3 governs and the result is alphanumeric, so the same MOVE must still be ACCEPTED. A fix that promotes whenever ANY argument is national would be an over-rejection, and a fix that only relabels would fail on the value.
rows.actual: The promotion is real, keys on argument-1, and carries the VALUE. rfc1 (national LITERALS: MOVE FUNCTION CONCAT(N"PQ" N"RS") TO PIC X(20)) -> 'error COBOLNET0819: MOVE . TO R: MOVE is invalid - a national sending operand does not move to an alphabetic, alphanumeric or alphanumeric-edited receiver (ISO 14.9.25.3 SR10, Table 16; FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF is the sanctioned conversion)', exit 70. rfc2 (national arg-1 + ALPHANUMERIC arg-2, CONCAT(NA B)) -> same COBOLNET0819, exit 70. rfc4 (NESTED: MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(FUNCTION CONCAT(NA NB)) TO PIC X(20)) -> same COBOLNET0819, exit 70. rfc5 (r4's THREE-argument iteration form into an ALPHABETIC receiver PIC A(20)) -> same COBOLNET0819, exit 70. OVER-REJECTION CONTROL rfc3 (alphanumeric arg-1 + national arg-2, CONCAT(A NB) -> PIC X(20)) -> compiles and prints ANUM1=[AB RS               ], exit 0 -- correctly NOT promoted. VALUE CONTROL rfc6 -> LITVAL=[PQRS        ], THREEVAL=[PQ RSTU     ] and IFNAT-TRUE (IF FUNCTION CONCAT(NA NB) = N"PQ RS"), exit 0.
rows.derivation: 15.18.4 r2 quoted above, with 15.18.4 r1 ('The returned value of the function shall contain all of the characters in argument-1 followed by all of the characters in argument-2') fixing the expected VALUES: NA is PIC N(3) so its image is 'PQ ' and CONCAT(NA NB NC) is 'PQ ' + 'RS' + 'TU' = 'PQ RSTU', while the two-character literals give 'PQ'+'RS' = 'PQRS' -- both measured exactly. 14.9.25.3 SR10 Table 16 supplies the rejection. The recorded defect was that IntrinsicCatalog fixed CONCAT's row at IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric unconditionally, so MoveBinder read a mislabelled sender category; the refuting question is whether the new label is CONDITIONAL on argument-1 (correct) or blanket (an over-rejection), and whether it is only a label.

rows.derivation: Re-derived independently from the spec text I read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.26.4: r2 = 'If argument-2 is specified, the alphanumeric substitution character is returned for each national character in argument-1 that has no corresponding alphanumeric character representation.' Legality of a figurative argument-2: 15.3 argument type 2 admits an alphanumeric literal; 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 admits a figurative constant wherever a rule allows a literal; 8.3.3.6.4 GR3 b fixes its length at one character; 15.26.3 r2 then requires exactly one character position, which SPACE is. So the required return is 'A B' - three character positions, the middle one U+0020. The ORD calibration is internal to the probe: ORD returns collating position = code point + 1 (ORD of 'A' printed 000066), so U+0020 must print 000033 and the r3 '?' would print 000064; the two are therefore distinguishable, which a bracketed display alone is not.

rows.expected: SS15.27.3 r3 fixes FUNCTION E under standard-decimal at exactly 2.718281828459045235360287471352662, and SS15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to EQUAL that equivalent arithmetic expression. SS8.4.3.2.3 r1 bars a function-identifier only as a RECEIVING operand and SS14.9.25.3 r3 makes identifier-1 of a MOVE a SENDING operand, so `MOVE FUNCTION E TO <numeric item>` is conforming source and must deliver that same value.
rows.actual: The COMPUTE channel is indeed fixed (rfesdb: `FUNCTION E + 0` into PIC 9V9(30) gives 2718281828459045235360287471352, ROUNDED gives ...353, DISPLAY gives the full 2.718281828459045235360287471352662). But the MOVE channel of the same constant NO LONGER COMPILES: `MOVE FUNCTION E TO R30` under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` fails the backend with `error: backend compilation failed (generated C# at rfesda.g.cs): (43,42): error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDec' to 'System.Int128'`, exit 70. The same MOVE under NATIVE arithmetic compiles and runs (rfesdc: 2718281828459045010062878703616), and the failure reproduces for every fixed-point receiver shape tried - PIC 9V9(30), PIC 9(3), PIC 9V9(9) COMP-3 - and under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` at --std 2014 as well as STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2023. A COMP-2 receiver is the only MOVE that survives.
rows.derivation: SS15.27.3 3) (--check OK) 'If standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect, the equivalent arithmetic expression is the exact value of the arithmetic expression (2.7182818284590452353602874713 52662)'; SS15.4.1 1) (--check OK) 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'. Legality of the failing source: SS8.4.3.2.3 1) (--check OK) 'A function-identifier shall not be specified as a receiving operand' - only receiving is barred; SS14.9.25.3 3) (--check OK) 'Literal-1 and the data item referenced by identifier-1 are sending operands'; SS8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 is the function-identifier. A rule whose value cannot be obtained at all in a legal channel is not satisfied in that channel, and SS4.2.2's warning mechanism is about violations of the standard - not a licence to emit ill-typed C#.
rows.probe: rfesda.cob: `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` / `01 R30 PIC 9V9(30).` / `MOVE FUNCTION E TO R30. DISPLAY "MOVE-R30 =" R30.` -> CS1503, exit 70. Controls: rfesdb.cob (the COMPUTE/ROUNDED/DISPLAY arms alone, exit 0 and exact); rfesdc.cob (the same MOVE under native, exit 0); rfech4/rfech5 (PIC 9(3) and COMP-3 receivers, both CS1503); rfech6 at --std 2014 under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` (CS1503); rfech3 (MOVE into COMP-2, exit 0). Generated line: `R30 = CobolNum.Store(CobolDec.E, 0, _P_0);` against the working COMPUTE emission `CobolNum.Store(CobolDec.Add(CobolDec.E, ...), _P_1, CobolRounding.Truncation)`.
variations: STATEMENT CHANNEL under the standard mode, which the prober held at COMPUTE and a relation condition: MOVE (fails to build), ADD (works, 3.718281828), STRING (works, full exact constant), DISPLAY (works)
RECEIVER KIND on the failing channel: PIC 9V9(30), PIC 9(3) integer, PIC 9V9(9) COMP-3 all fail; COMP-2 alone succeeds
ARITHMETIC MODE and EDITION on the failing channel: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` at --std 2014 fails identically, so it is not a STANDARD-DECIMAL-only or 2023-only artifact
rows.mechanism: Emitter - R18's standard-mode arm runs before the float dispatch in `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum` and yields a `CobolDec` (`CobolDec.E` / `CobolDec.Pi` / `CobolDec.Pow`), but the MOVE store path selects the scaled-integer overload `CobolNum.Store(Int128 raw, int scale, PicInfo)` and is handed the CobolDec, so the emitter writes an ill-typed call and Roslyn rejects the generated program. The COMPUTE path selects `Store(CobolDec, PicInfo, CobolRounding)` and is fine. Scope measured, not assumed: exactly the FOUR functions R18 folded - E, PI, EXP, EXP10 - fail this way, while SQRT, LOG, FACTORIAL and ABS all MOVE cleanly under the same OPTIONS paragraph. One fix, one site; it closes this row and RV-15.73.3-3 and the standard half of RV-15.34.4-1.

The antecedent quantifies over THE condition associated with the last exception status, so what any OTHER co-enabled condition's directive said is irrelevant; the implementor's documented 7.3.25.4 GR7 answer is to save none. 7.3.25.4 GR3 additionally makes a level-2 exception-name 'as if that TURN directive were specified containing all exception-names that are subordinate', so a level-2 directive carrying LOCATION must yield the FULL r2 b) string for a subordinate level-3 condition -- the complement of r1, and the axis rxa4 measures.

rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo3.cob runs Annex D.31.5.7's own arguments (143951, 18867.812479168304, +300) over "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm" through a COMP-2 item and through a PIC 9(5)V9(12) control in one program and prints FLT=[19950215T05142781+0500], FIX=[19950215T05142781+0500], D31=SAME - the annex's value, bit for bit, from both storage shapes. rfo4.cob shows the national result refused by PIC X(40) and rfb4.cob shows it delivered into PIC N(24). rfo8.cob renders an 18-'s' fraction as F18=[20260809T093320546632700000000000] (real digits, no sign character) and rfo2.cob rejects a 19-'s' fraction with COBOLNET1631. VARIATION 1 (the format-class screen, per function and in both directions - never probed): rfk2.cob shows FORMATTED-DATETIME refusing a DATE-only format ('argument-1 is 'YYYYMMDD', which is a DATE format; this function admits COMBINED date-and-time (ISO §15.40.3 r2)') and a TIME-only format, while FORMATTED-DATE refuses a COMBINED format (15.39.3 r2) and FORMATTED-TIME refuses a COMBINED format (15.41.3 r2) - four diagnostics, each naming its own function's r2. VARIATION 2 (fraction disposition across widths, never measured): rfk1.cob renders argument-3 = 18867.996 at width 2 as TRUNC2=[19950215T05142799] (truncation, not rounding - a rounding implementation would have had to carry into the seconds subfield), 18867.125 at width 6 as WIDE6=[19950215T051427125000] and at width 1 as NARROW1=[19950215T0514271].
rows.derivation: 15.40.4 r1 read at line 31419: 'The returned value is a representation of the date contained in argument-2 combined with the time contained in argument-3 according to the format in argument-1.' A value whose fraction was dropped is not a representation of the time CONTAINED in argument-3; a value delivered under the wrong class is not the representation 15.40.1's table names; and subfields rendered from a format that is not a combined date-and-time format are not representations of the arguments at all - which is why r2's screen is part of this rule's evidence and why it must be per-function (the same string is legal for one function and illegal for another, so a single global recogniser would have to get all three wrong or all three right). 15.3.3.2 requires the implementor to define the maximum fraction width and requires it to be >= 9; docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.1 item 202 defines it as 18, so 18 must render and 19 must be diagnosed. 15.3.3.2 does NOT settle truncation versus rounding, so the measured truncation is implementor latitude and is recorded, not graded.
rows.probe: rfo3.cob (D.31.5.7 through COMP-2 and fixed-point with an in-program IF); rfk2.cob (date-only and time-only formats for FORMATTED-DATETIME, combined format for FORMATTED-DATE and FORMATTED-TIME); rfk1.cob (fraction widths 1, 2 and 6); rfo8.cob and rfo2.cob (fraction widths 18 and 19); rfo4.cob / rfb4.cob (national result, both receiver directions). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: FORMAT-CLASS SCREEN, PER FUNCTION AND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - the prober probed only a malformed format ('MMDDThhmmss'). A WELL-FORMED format of the wrong CLASS is the harder case, and each of the three functions refuses exactly the classes its own r2 excludes while accepting its own; a shared recogniser without per-function classification could not produce that pattern.

FRACTION-DISPOSITION AND WIDTH AXIS - the original note recorded the truncation-versus-rounding question as UNVERIFIED and no probe had settled it. Measured: truncation, at widths 1, 2 and 6, with zero-extension when the format is wider than the value's scale. Not graded as a defect - 15.3.3.2 leaves it to the implementor - but recorded so the question is closed.
STORAGE-SHAPE CONTROL against the standard's own worked value, re-run independently: COMP-2 and fixed-point agree AND both equal D.31.5.7.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md (landed) for the float channel, kb/Work/PB15.md (landed) for the result type, kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) plus docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.1 item 202 for the format recogniser and the fraction cap; all re-verified, the recogniser now also on well-formed-but-wrong-class formats.

rows.expected: When the UTC adjustment moves the date outside 15.5.2's range the conforming behaviour is EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION plus the implementor-defined result - and, equally, when the adjustment moves the date WITHIN range the roll shall still happen and produce the adjusted date.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo5.cob (3067671, 86399, -1439 - every argument individually legal) aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the UTC adjustment (§15.40.4 r2) moves the date to integer date form 3067672, outside 1..3,067,671 (§15.5.2) - the year would leave the §15.3.1.3 range 1601..9999', exit 1; rfo6.cob (1, 0, +1439) aborts with the same diagnostic naming 'integer date form 0', exit 1. VARIATION 1 (LEGAL ROLLS - the over-rejection axis, never probed): rfl1.cob runs five cases under checking ON and completes, exit 0: ROLLUP=[19950216T005959Z] (143951, 86399, -60 - the roll carries the date FORWARD one day), ROLLDN=[19950214T230000Z] (143951, 0, +60 - the roll carries it BACK one day), NOROLL=[19950215T123456Z], TOPOK=[99991231T000059Z] (3067671, 86399, +1439 - adjustment at the top endpoint that stays in range) and BOTOK=[16010101T235900Z] (1, 0, -1439 - the same at the bottom endpoint), then REACHED-END. VARIATION 2 (checking OFF): covered by rfd3/rfh2 for the sibling guards; the diagnostic's own wording locates this one at the roll rather than at entry.
rows.derivation: 15.40.4 r2 read at line 31421: 'If the format in argument-1 indicates that the returned value is to be expressed in UTC, the time portion of the returned value reflects the adjustment of the value in argument-3 by the offset in argument-4.' 15.3.3.6.1 item 1 (line 29719) fixes the direction - a plus sign means the common time portion 'is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC' - so a NEGATIVE argument-4 adds. I recomputed each case: 86399 + 86340 = 172739 >= 86400 so the top case rolls to integer date 3067672, one past 15.5.2's maximum; 0 - 86340 < 0 so the bottom case rolls to 0; 86399 + 3600 = 89999 rolls forward one day to 1995-02-16 at 00:59:59; 0 - 3600 rolls back one day to 1995-02-14 at 23:00:00; 86399 - 86340 = 59 and 0 + 86340 = 86340 both stay inside one day, so the two endpoint cases must NOT roll and must render 9999-12-31T00:00:59Z and 1601-01-01T23:59:00Z. The refutation risk this row carried above all others is that a guard added to stop the out-of-range roll could have suppressed the roll itself; every legal roll above is measured and correct, so it did not.
rows.probe: rfo5.cob (top end, checking ON); rfo6.cob (bottom end, checking ON); rfl1.cob (forward roll, backward roll, no roll, and adjustment at both 15.5.2 endpoints that stays in range - all under checking ON in one program). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: LEGAL-ROLL AXIS (over-rejection) - a guard that simply refused any date change would have passed both of the prober's probes and failed here. Rolls in both directions still occur and produce the correctly adjusted dates.

IN-RANGE ADJUSTMENT AT BOTH 15.5.2 ENDPOINTS - the maximal offset applied at integer date 3067671 and at integer date 1 in the direction that stays in range renders correctly, so the guard tests the POST-roll date rather than rejecting the endpoints outright.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R25.md (status: landed) for the reworked roll block and kb/Work/PB23.md (landed) for the EC-instead-of-CLR discipline; re-verified against the over-rejection hypothesis, which is the failure mode a guard-shaped fix most easily introduces.

rows.expected: Over an offset format, argument-3 shall be reflected DIRECTLY in the time portion (unadjusted, fraction intact) and argument-4 DIRECTLY in the offset portion, in both the basic and the extended offset subformat, for offsets that are not whole hours and for both signs.
rows.actual: ORIGINAL RE-RUN: rfo3.cob's COMP-2 argument-3 over "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm" prints FLT=[19950215T05142781+0500] - the time portion 05:14:27.81 is D.31.5.7's UNADJUSTED local time while +0500 sits in the offset portion, which is precisely how r3 differs from r2 (rfo5/rfl1 show the UTC format performing the r2 adjustment on the same machinery). VARIATION 1 (offsets that split into non-zero hours AND non-zero minutes, both signs, both subformats - never probed): rfm1.cob prints BAS-P345=[19950215T123456+0545], BAS-N345=[19950215T123456-0545], EXT-P345=[1995-02-15T12:34:56+05:45], EXT-N345=[1995-02-15T12:34:56-05:45]. The prober's probes used +05:00 (minutes zero) and -00:30 (hours zero), so neither exercised the 60-minute split with both fields non-zero. VARIATION 2 (fraction subfield combined with the extended offset subformat at the maximum legal magnitude): rfm1.cob prints EXT-FR-N1439=[1995-02-15T12:34:56.000-23:59] and BAS-1439=[19950215T123456+2359] - offset-hours stays inside 15.3.3.6.2's 00..23 at the extreme. VARIATION 3 (the note's defect (e) is genuinely unreachable): rfp2.cob shows "YYYYMMDDThhmmss+hhmmhh" - a further 'hh' run after an offset subformat, the exact shape the never-reset offset flag would mis-classify - rejected with COBOLNET1631.
rows.derivation: 15.40.4 r3 read at line 31423: 'If the format in argument-1 indicates that the time is to be returned as an offset from UTC, the value in argument-3 is reflected directly in the time portion of the returned value, and the offset in argument-4 is reflected directly in the offset portion of the returned value.' 'Directly' is the operative word twice. 15.3.3.6.1 fixes the subformat widths - five characters (+hhmm) basic, six (+hh:mm) extended - and 15.3.3.6.2 (line 29744) requires 'The offset-hours subfield ... shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive' and the offset-minutes subfield 00 to 59. 345 minutes = 5 h 45 m and 1439 = 23 h 59 m, so a correct implementation must print +0545 and +2359; an implementation that divided or formatted wrongly would show it only when BOTH fields are non-zero, which is why this is the discriminating case and why the prober's zero-in-one-field probes could not reach it. 45296 s = 12:34:56 and the time portion must be unchanged by the offset.
rows.probe: rfo3.cob (D.31.5.7 shape, float and fixed-point); rfm1.cob (+345, -345 in the basic and extended offset subformats; 1439 basic; -1439 with a 3-digit fraction in the extended subformat); rfp2.cob (trailing hh run after the offset subformat); rfl1.cob (the r2 contrast on a UTC format). Command: cobol.exe <src> --std 2023 -o <n>.dll --run
variations: NON-WHOLE-HOUR OFFSET AXIS, both signs, both subformats - +-345 exercises the /60 and %60 split with both fields non-zero, which the prober's +05:00 and -00:30 could not. All four render correctly.

EXTREME-MAGNITUDE-WITH-FRACTION AXIS - the maximum legal magnitude in the extended subformat alongside a fractional-seconds subfield renders .000-23:59, so the offset-hours field stays inside 15.3.3.6.2's range at the boundary and the fraction and offset subfields do not interfere.

DEFECT (e) REACHABILITY - the malformed shape the note said the never-reset offset flag would silently re-classify is rejected outright by the recogniser, so the constituent defect is closed by removal of its precondition rather than left latent.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md (landed) for the Real-blind and Dec-blind seconds channel and kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) for the magnitude guard, the range guard and the format recogniser; re-verified on the offset split that only a correct 60-minute division renders.

rows.expected: The returned value must represent argument-2's value for every legal argument-2 form (§15.3 type 10: an arithmetic expression or a numeric data item). The prober swept FLOAT-LONG / FLOAT-SHORT / COMP-2 / PIC 9V99 / literal and the fraction-width axis. The forms they never drove: a PACKED-DECIMAL (COMP-3) scaled item, an ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION as argument-2 (which reaches the renderer through a computed NumX, not a leaf Place), a SIGN LEADING SEPARATE item, and a format whose fraction is WIDER than the item's scale - the direction opposite to every case probed, where the renderer must pad rather than truncate.
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED on all five. r7v1: COMP3=[123456125] (`01 P3 PIC 9(5)V9(3) USAGE COMP-3 VALUE 45296.125.` under "hhmmss.sss"); EXPRDIV=[12345650] (`FL / 2` with `01 FL USAGE FLOAT-LONG VALUE 90593.0.` under "hhmmss.ss" - a fractional result produced by DIVISION, not by a stored fraction); WIDEFMT=[1234565000] (`01 D2 PIC 9(5)V99 VALUE 45296.50.` under the WIDER "hhmmss.ssss", correctly zero-padded, not garbage); SIGNSEP=[12345625] (`01 SG PIC S9(5)V99 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE VALUE 45296.25.`); EXPRADD=[12345675] (`D2 + 0.25`). No truncation of a fraction, no wrap, no OverflowException on any channel.
rows.derivation: §15.41.4 1) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31468) 'The returned value is a representation of the standard numeric time contained in argument-2 according to the format in argument-1.' §15.6's Table 21 types argument-2 'Num2' = §15.3 type 10, 'An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified', so a COMP-3 item, a SIGN SEPARATE item and the value of an arithmetic expression are all legal argument-2 and their value must be represented. 45296.125 is 12:34:56.125 -> 123456125 at three fraction digits; 90593.0/2 = 45296.5 -> 12345650; 45296.50 under a four-digit fraction is 1234565000 because §15.3.3.2's fraction subfield is a fixed-width digit string, so the missing low-order digits are zeros.
rows.probe: r7v1.cob (RFT1441V1) drives all five in one program: `MOVE FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss.sss", P3)`, `("hhmmss.ss", FL / 2)`, `("hhmmss.ssss", D2)`, `("hhmmss.ss", SG)`, `("hhmmss.ss", D2 + 0.25)`. Command: cobol.exe r7v1.cob --std 2023 -o r7v1.dll --run. Output: COMP3=[123456125] / EXPRDIV=[12345650] / WIDEFMT=[1234565000] / SIGNSEP=[12345625] / EXPRADD=[12345675].
variations: PACKED-DECIMAL (COMP-3) scaled argument-2 - a USAGE the prober never drove, and the one most likely to have its own Place arm.

ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION as argument-2, including a DIVISION that manufactures the fraction (`FL / 2`) and an ADDITION (`D2 + 0.25`): the prober used only stored values and literals, so the computed-NumX path was untested.
FRACTION WIDER THAN THE ITEM'S SCALE ("hhmmss.ssss" over a V99 item) - the opposite direction to every probed case; the renderer pads with zeros rather than mis-scaling.
SIGN LEADING SEPARATE fixed-point argument-2: correct, so the sign-storage variants of the DISPLAY leaf agree with the plain one.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md (landed) for the Real/Dec value channel; kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) + docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 202 for the fraction-width maximum. The prober's attribution stands.

rows.expected: With a UTC format the time portion must reflect argument-2 adjusted by argument-3 (UTC = local - offset per §15.3.3.6.1 items 1 and 2). The prober varied polarity and fraction width but supplied argument-3 ONLY as a signed numeric LITERAL and never crossed midnight in either direction - so the two shapes left untested are (i) argument-3 as a signed DATA ITEM, and (ii) an adjustment that drives the adjusted value OUT of [0, 86400) and must be normalized back, which is precisely the code the original note said the omit path skipped. A national UTC format is a third untested arm.
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED, and the normalization is right in both directions. r8v1: ROLLDOWN=[23:00:00Z] for ("hh:mm:ssZ", 3600, O1) with `01 O1 PIC S9(4) VALUE 120.` - 3600 - 7200 = -3600, +86400 = 82800 = 23:00:00, so the underflow rolls back a day correctly. ROLLUP=[01:00:00Z] for ("hh:mm:ssZ", 82800, O2) with `01 O2 PIC S9(4) VALUE -120.` - 82800 + 7200 = 90000, -86400 = 3600 = 01:00:00, the overflow rolls forward. NATUTC=[14:34:56Z] for (N"hh:mm:ssZ", 45296, -120) = 45296 + 7200 = 52496. ITEMPOS=[10:34:56Z] for the same call with argument-3 as the DATA ITEM O1 = +120 (45296 - 7200 = 38096). MAXOFF=[12:35:56Z] at the +1439 boundary (45296 - 86340 = -41044, +86400 = 45356 = 12:35:56).
rows.derivation: §15.41.4 2) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31470) 'If the format in argument-1 indicates that the returned value is to be expressed in UTC, the time portion of the returned value reflects the adjustment of the value in argument-2 by the offset in argument-3.' §15.3.3.6.1 item 1 makes a plus offset an adjustment DOWNWARD to reach UTC and item 2 an adjustment UPWARD, i.e. UTC = local - offset. The returned value must still be a time of day, so an adjusted value outside [0, 86400) is normalized modulo a day - which is what makes the roll cases the sharp test. I computed each expected string by hand from those two rules before running.
rows.probe: r8v1.cob (RFT1442V1): `01 O1 PIC S9(4) VALUE 120.` / `01 O2 PIC S9(4) VALUE -120.` driving ("hh:mm:ssZ", 3600, O1), ("hh:mm:ssZ", 82800, O2), (N"hh:mm:ssZ", 45296, -120) into PIC N(20) read back with FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF, ("hh:mm:ssZ", 45296, O1) and ("hh:mm:ssZ", 45296, 1439). Command: cobol.exe r8v1.cob --std 2023 -o r8v1.dll --run. Outputs verbatim in 'actual'.
variations: MIDNIGHT ROLL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS - the axis nothing in the prober's set or the recorded corpus touched: a positive offset that underflows past 00:00:00 and a negative offset that overflows past 24:00:00 both normalize correctly.
argument-3 AS A SIGNED DATA ITEM rather than a literal, in both signs: the prober used literals exclusively, so a fold-time-only adjustment would have shown here.
NATIONAL UTC format literal, exercising §15.41.1's National->National return arm together with the adjustment.
MAGNITUDE BOUNDARY +1439 combined with the adjustment (not merely accepted, but arithmetically checked: 12:35:56Z).
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md + kb/Work/PB11.md + kb/Work/R25.md (all landed). The prober's attribution stands.

rows.expected: A conjunctive rule: with an offset format, argument-2 goes DIRECTLY into the time portion (no UTC adjustment) AND argument-3 DIRECTLY into the offset portion. The prober checked mid-range argument-2 values only, so the untested axes are (i) argument-2 at the extremes of [0, 86400) combined with a large negative offset - the case where a leaked adjustment would visibly wrap the time portion - (ii) argument-3 as a signed DATA ITEM, and (iii) the |argument-3| = 1439 boundary in the EXTENDED subformat, where §15.3.3.6.2 caps offset-hours at 23.
rows.actual: CONFIRMED FIXED. r9v1: EDGE-NOADJ=[235959-0500] for ("hhmmss+hhmm", 86399, O2) with `01 O2 PIC S9(4) VALUE -300.` - the time portion is 23:59:59 unchanged, so NO adjustment leaked in at the top of the range (an adjustment would have produced 01:59:59 or a wrap). ZEROTIME=[000000-0500] for the same offset at argument-2 = 0 - unchanged at the bottom of the range too. EXT-MAX=[12:34:56+23:59] and EXT-MIN=[12:34:56-23:59] at +/-1439 in the extended subformat: offset-hours 23, inside §15.3.3.6.2's 00..23, with the colon coming from the format. Both halves of the conjunction hold.
rows.derivation: §15.41.4 3) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31473) 'If the format in argument-1 indicates that the time is to be returned as an offset from UTC, the value in argument-2 is reflected directly in the time portion of the returned value, and the offset in argument-3 is reflected directly in the offset portion of the returned value.' 'Directly' for the time portion means the §15.41.4 2) adjustment must NOT be applied - which is only observable if a leaked adjustment would change the digits, hence testing at 86399 with a -300 offset (a leak would give 01:59:59) and at 0 (a leak would give 05:00:00). §15.3.3.6.1 gives the offset subformat sign + hh + mm, with the extended form's colon carried in the data; §15.3.3.6.2 caps offset-hours at 23, and 1439 minutes = 23 h 59 min renders +/-23:59.
rows.probe: r9v1.cob (RFT1443V1): `01 O2 PIC S9(4) VALUE -300.` driving ("hhmmss+hhmm", 86399, O2), ("hh:mm:ss+hh:mm", 45296, 1439), ("hh:mm:ss+hh:mm", 45296, -1439) and ("hhmmss+hhmm", 0, O2). Command: cobol.exe r9v1.cob --std 2023 -o r9v1.dll --run. Output: EDGE-NOADJ=[235959-0500] / EXT-MAX=[12:34:56+23:59] / EXT-MIN=[12:34:56-23:59] / ZEROTIME=[000000-0500].
variations: argument-2 AT BOTH EXTREMES of the legal interval (86399 and 0) with a nonzero offset - the shape that makes a leaked UTC adjustment visible; the prober only ever used mid-range values where a leak is still a plausible-looking time.
argument-3 AS A SIGNED DATA ITEM (the prober used only literals for the offset here).

|argument-3| = 1439 IN THE EXTENDED SUBFORMAT, checked against §15.3.3.6.2's 00..23 offset-hours cap rather than merely 'accepted' - the recorded defect's own failure mode was an offset-hours field of 33.
rows.attribution: kb/Work/R24.md (landed) for the value channel; kb/Work/PB11.md (landed) for the offset bound. The prober's attribution stands.

rows.expected: Under STANDARD-DECIMAL the returned value shall EQUAL the EAE (argument-1 - FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(argument-1)), for either sign and either carrier, and 15.4.1 NOTE 2's relation condition shall therefore evaluate TRUE.

rows.derivation: 15.42.4 1) at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31500-31504 - 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is: (argument-1 - FUNCTION INTEGER-PART (argument-1)) where the argument for the INTEGER-PART function is the same as for the FRACTION-PART function itself.' 15.4.1 1) at 29795 - 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression.' 15.4.1 NOTE 2 - the relation 'function-identifier = equivalent-arithmetic-expression' will evaluate to true. 8.8.1.5.1 lifts a float operand into SDIDI via its decimal form, so the fraction of 1234567890.123 is exactly 0.123.
rows.probe: rf03a.cob (RF03A): OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. / 01 DNEG USAGE COMP-2 VALUE -1234567890.123 / 01 FX PIC S9(9)V9(9) VALUE 123.456789012 / 01 R PIC S9V9(9) SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE; COMPUTE + the NOTE 2 relation for each carrier. cmd: cobol.exe rf03a.cob --std 2023 -o rf03a.dll --run

the 15.4.1 NOTE 2 RELATION-CONDITION channel, which the prober never used - the hand-written EAE and the function-identifier now agree in the comparison itself, not merely after storing into a receiver

rows.expected: §15.43.4 r1 constrains exactly one construct — 'When argument-1 is a floating-point numeric-edited item, the data description entry ... shall be such that, if argument-1 contained the positive value farthest from zero ... an IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE test of argument-1 would return a true value.' The domain is an external floating-point PICTURE (symbol E); if that cannot be declared, the rule cannot be reached.
rows.actual: The construct still does not compile. 01 E1 PIC -9.9(5)E+99. -> 'error COBOLNET0899: an external floating-point PICTURE (symbol E) is recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 6) — data item E1 (ISO §13.18.40 external float; skeleton W2 (loud), full Phase 6 (IEEE float catchall); PENDING)', followed by 'error COBOLNET1516: FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC argument-1 shall be a category numeric or numeric-edited DATA ITEM ...' because the item never acquires PicCategory.NumericEdited. exit=70. The rule's other half is also still absent: the well-formedness test it prescribes is an IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE class condition, and nothing in the compiler relates any ALGEBRAIC fold to such a test.
rows.derivation: §15.43.4 r1 read verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31548. Both of the rule's halves — the floating-point numeric-edited DOMAIN and the IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE TEST — must exist for the rule to be implementable; the probe shows the domain is staged not-implemented, so this is a genuine unimplemented rule whose zero fan-out merely looks green.
rows.probe: p434a.cob (PHA434A): 01 E1 PIC -9.9(5)E+99. / 01 RE PIC +99999999.999. / MOVE FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(E1) TO RE / DISPLAY "EFLT=" RE. Command: cobol.exe p434a.cob --std 2023 -o p434a.dll --run

rows.expected: §15.45.4 r1 a)/b)/c): argument-1 is assigned to a temporary boolean item 'described with the same number of boolean positions as argument-1', then 'the unsigned binary value represented by the same bit configuration' of that temporary is the returned value. For a 64-position all-ones argument that value is 18446744073709551615, and for 70 positions it is 1180591620717411303423 — both exactly representable in a PIC 9(31) receiver. §15.4 does permit an implementor maximum with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, but §A.1 item 93 makes DOCUMENTING that maximum mandatory.
rows.actual: The edge the note named reproduces unchanged. 63 one-bits -> B63=0000000000009223372036854775807 (2^63-1, correct). 64 one-bits -> B64=0000000000000000000000000000000. 70 one-bits -> B70=0000000000000000000000000000000. exit=0 in every case: with EC checking off (the default) the argument error silently returns ZERO, so a program whose receiver can hold the exact answer instead receives 0 with no diagnostic and no exception. The cap is still 63 bits — below the compiler's own 31-digit fixed-point channel and below §8.3.3.4.3 SR1's 8 191 boolean positions — and it is still undocumented: grep of docs/CONFORMANCE.md finds no §A.1 item-93 returned-value-length row and no mention of INTEGER-OF-BOOLEAN.
rows.derivation: §15.45.4 r1 read verbatim at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:31637-31645. Subrule 1a ties the temporary's width to argument-1's own width, so a 70-position item has a 70-position temporary and 1b's unsigned value follows arithmetically; nothing in §15.45.4 authorises truncation. The §15.4 escape is about the LENGTH of a returned value and is legitimate in SHAPE, which is why this row is PARTIAL rather than a flat wrong answer — but the silent zero (not the EC) is what a user sees by default, and §A.1 item 93's documentation obligation is unmet, so the row does not close.

rows.derivation: 15.50.4 rule 1, quoted: "If argument-1 is a bit group item, an elementary boolean data item, a boolean literal, or a type declaration for a boolean item, the returned value is an integer equal to the length of argument-1 in boolean positions." Boolean positions are counted per 3.24 ('boolean position <storage required> amount of physical storage required to store ... a single boolean character'), so B"1011" is 4 and PIC 1(3) is 3 regardless of usage - which is why USAGE BIT must still answer 5, not ceil(5/8).

rows.expected: r9 rounds UP only when the answer is in alphanumeric character positions AND argument-1 does not occupy an integral number of them. Axes the prober did not vary: (i) the NEGATIVE precondition inside an alphanumeric group - `01 EB. 05 E1 PIC 1(4) BIT. 05 E2 PIC 1(4) BIT.` occupies EXACTLY one position, so r9 must not fire and the answer is 1, not 2; (ii) a group of THREE bit siblings occupying 9/8 positions -> 2; (iii) a bit item one level DEEPER, `01 NG1. 05 SUBG. 10 NB PIC 1(3) BIT. 10 NA PIC X.` -> 2; (iv) a bit item packed against a COMP item -> 3; (v) a LEVEL 77 bit item, whose answer is in BOOLEAN positions under r1 and must therefore NOT be rounded -> 5.
rows.actual: r01 -> EBLN=1, TBLN=2, NG1LN=2, BCLN=3, SVBLN=5. The exactly-integral case is the one that separates r9 from a blanket ceiling and it is right (1, not 2), and the level-77 control shows the rounding is not applied where the answer is not in alphanumeric positions (5, not 1). The recorded PREMISE - that no representation ever occupies a fractional position, so r9 was unreachable - is false on this compiler, and where it is now reachable it rounds correctly and only there.
rows.derivation: 15.50.4 r9, quoted: "When the returned value is expressed as a number of alphanumeric character positions and argument-1 does not occupy an integral number of positions, the returned value is rounded to the next larger integer value." Two conditions, both necessary. For an alphanumeric group r3 puts the answer in alphanumeric positions, so condition one holds and the occupancy decides: 8 bits is exactly one position (no rounding, 1), 9 bits is 1.125 (rounds to 2), and 3 bits under a deeper group plus a byte is 1.375 (rounds to 2). For an elementary boolean item r1 puts the answer in BOOLEAN positions, so condition one FAILS and 5 boolean positions stay 5 - the complement that makes the rule a rule rather than a ceiling.

rows.derivation: Re-derived from the text I read at §15.57.4: r1 = 'A character string with the content of argument-1 is returned, with any uppercase letters replaced by their corresponding lowercase letters.' Admissibility: 15.57.3 r1 requires class alphabetic/alphanumeric/national and at least one character position; 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 admits a figurative wherever a rule allows a literal, 8.3.3.6.4 GR1 gives it an alphanumeric character value and GR3 b length one, GR3 c gives ALL literal-1 the length of literal-1. So LOWER-CASE(SPACE) must return one character equal to the argument's (U+0020, ORD 000033) and LOWER-CASE(ALL "AB") must return 'ab' of length 2. Measuring LENGTH is load-bearing: a padded receiver renders an EMPTY return and a correct one identically, and an empty return would violate r1 just as an abort does.

XCOMP CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION IS USER-DEFAULT.) compiles EXIT=0 with NO diagnostic at all and LOWER-CASE returns the rule-4 invariant fold: LC-CLASSIF=[abcde   ]. P57433 (CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION then PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS MYALPH) likewise EXIT=0, ORDER-A=[abcde   ]. rows.derivation: 15.57.4 r3 verbatim: 'When locale-name-1 is not specified and a locale is in effect for character classification, as described in 12.3.6, OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph, the correspondence of uppercase to lowercase letters is determined from locale category LC_CTYPE.' The clause is the ONLY way to satisfy r3's antecedent, so accepting it and discarding it makes r3 silently unsatisfiable while the program has asked for it - the one place in the A.4.9 disposition where the refusal is not loud, and the harm lands exactly on this rule. rows.expected: 15.64.4 1): the returned value is ((argument-1) - ((argument-2) * FUNCTION INTEGER ((argument-1) / (argument-2)))). For A PIC S9(18) VALUE 999999999999999 and B PIC S9(18) VALUE 1000000007, argument-1 = A ** 2 = 999999999999998000000000000001 (30 digits) and the value owed is 13657001 (independent oracle: python -c "print(999999999999999**2 % 1000000007)" -> 13657001). That value fits every receiver used. A ** 2 over an integer item is 'an arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value' (15.3 6), so it is a fully LEGAL argument; 15.2 5) makes MOD an integer function with no digits to the right of the decimal point; and 15.4 makes the returned value a property of the FUNCTION, so it may not vary with the statement context or with the receiver's PICTURE.
rows.actual: The prober's FIXED is correct only at the ONE magnitude the note happened to pin. At a larger legal magnitude the divergence is not gone - it has SWAPPED ARMS, and the value is now wrong in the receiver-bearing COMPUTE that used to be the correct arm. r6441h.cob (RF6441H), --std 2023, compiled with ZERO diagnostics: 'H COMPUTE   = +000000000320612800' (WRONG; 13657001 owed) with its ON SIZE ERROR arm SILENT, 'H DISPLAY   = 13657001' (correct) and 'H IF        = RIGHT'. Byte-identical at --std 85, 2002 and 2014. THE RECEIVER'S PICTURE ALONE DECIDES THE VALUE - r6441w.cob (RF6441W) runs the identical 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B)' four times into four receivers: 'RCV S9(9)  = +320612800', 'RCV S9(18) = +000000000320612800', 'RCV S9(28) = +0000000000000000000320612800', 'RCV S9(31) = +0000000000000000000000013657001'. One statement, one pair of arguments, two different answers selected by the receiver's width - the very invariant the PB32 comment block in NumericRenderer.cs claims to have restored ('A function's value must not depend on the SHAPE of its receiver'). ATTRIBUTABLE CONTROLS, all in r6441c.cob (RF6441C), same run unit, same magnitude: 'C POW WIDE  = +0999999999999998000000000000001' (the exponentiation itself is EXACT, so the power is not the culprit); 'C MOD A*A   = +000000000013657001' (the same magnitude via A * A is CORRECT, so the magnitude is not out of range); 'C MOD ITEM  = +000000000013657001' (the same magnitude passed as a 31-digit DATA ITEM is CORRECT, so only the exponentiation-ARGUMENT route is broken). BOUNDARY - r6441b.cob (RF6441B): 13 nines -> 900139973 (correct), 14 nines -> 1396571 (correct), 15 nines -> 320612800 (WRONG, 13657001 owed), no ON SIZE ERROR on any of them. SIBLING - r6441r.cob (RF6441R): REM at the same magnitude gives 'REM COMPUTE = +000000000320612800' vs 'REM DISPLAY = 13657001' and 'REM MULT    = +000000000013657001', so 15.77.4 carries it too. WHAT THE PROBER SAW IS REPRODUCED AND IS NOT DISPUTED: r6441a.cob (RF6441A) prints 'MOD COMPUTE = +000000000930000007', 'MOD DISPLAY = 930000007', 'IF COND     = RIGHT', and r6441n/r6441s show nested-function, EVALUATE, PERFORM-UNTIL, scaled-receiver, COMP-2-receiver and all four 15.64.4 NOTE sign rows correct at the small magnitudes. The row is STILL-LIVE because the RULE is still violated on legal source, not because the prober's probes failed.
rows.derivation: cite.py --check 15.64.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is" -> OK 15.64.4 1); the formula read directly at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.64.4 ('((argument-1) - ((argument-2) * FUNCTION INTEGER ((argument-1) / (argument-2))))') with the NOTE table 11/5->1, -11/5->4, 11/-5->-4, -11/-5->-1. cite.py --check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified." -> OK 15.3 6) establishes A ** 2 as a legal argument. cite.py --check 15.2 "An integer function has an operational sign and no digits to the right of the decimal point." -> OK 15.2 5) is what makes a nine-digit-scaled intermediate a rule violation and not a display artefact. Expected values computed independently in python (%), never from the compiler.

THE OVERTURN: r6441h.cob (RF6441H) '01 A PIC S9(18) VALUE 999999999999999. 01 B PIC S9(18) VALUE 1000000007. 01 R PIC S9(18) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE.' + 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B) ON SIZE ERROR DISPLAY "H-SIZEERR-COMPUTE" END-COMPUTE' + 'DISPLAY FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B)' + 'IF FUNCTION MOD(A ** 2, B) = 13657001'. r6441w.cob (RF6441W): the same COMPUTE into PIC S9(9) / S9(18) / S9(28) / S9(31) receivers. r6441c.cob (RF6441C): the three attributable controls (A ** 2 into PIC S9(31); FUNCTION MOD(A * A, B); FUNCTION MOD(W, B) with W the 31-digit item). r6441b.cob (RF6441B): the 13/14/15-nines boundary. r6441r.cob (RF6441R): the REM sibling. r6441a.cob / r6441n.cob / r6441s.cob: the prober's shape plus the nested-function, EVALUATE, PERFORM-UNTIL, scaled-receiver, float-receiver and four-sign-row variations.

rows.mechanism: NumericRenderer.cs#Power's receiver-BEARING arm renders an integer-operand '**' as PowNativeInt(b, e, pscale) with pscale = ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale = max(receiver scale, the 9 float floor) capped at the receiver's Int128 headroom, so 'A ** 2' arrives at IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's 'case "ModScaled": case "RemScaled":' arm at SCALE 9 (and MOD's own 's = Math.Max(a.Scale, b.Scale)' keeps it there, which is also the 15.2 r5 violation the note charged); the 30-digit exact value times 10^9 is 39 digits and exceeds Int128, so the scaled carrier is corrupted before ModScaled ever runs - while the RECEIVER-LESS arm now takes pscale = 0 and stays exact, and a PIC S9(31) receiver drops the headroom cap to 7 and lands back inside Int128, which is exactly the S9(28)-wrong / S9(31)-right split measured in r6441w. PB32 fixed the receiver-less arm; the fixed-receiver arm's forced scale-9 was left, so the receiver-shape dependence survived with its arms swapped.
rows.attribution: The prober's attribution (kb/Work/PB32.md + kb/Work/PB38.md, both landed) is correct for the HALF that landed - the receiver-less/float-routing half. The surviving half is unattributed and appears to be new residue of PB13/PB32's FloatWorkingScale rule rather than of the original ModReal defect.

The determination is still recorded nowhere: docs/CONFORMANCE.md has NO row for A.1 item 132 or 133 (grep of `^\| 13[23] \|` returns nothing; only item 135 exists). And src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/ModuleStack.cs line 49 still documents Name() as returning the value "trimmed (a dynamic-length result -- r1, no trailing spaces)", which its own STACK arm contradicts.
rows.derivation: 15.65.4 r1 (spec line 32467): "If the implementation supports dynamic length elementary items, then the returned value is an alphanumeric dynamic length elementary item with no trailing spaces, except that if the function is specified in a COBOL main program and the ACTIVATING keyword is specified, then a single space is returned. If the implementation supports more than one type of dynamic length elementary items, then the implementor shall document which type is used." The exception clause is singular and names only main-program ACTIVATING; every other returned value must carry no trailing space. STACK ends in one because r9 requires a final single-space entry, so the two rules collide and the collision is exactly what has to be recorded -- r1's own last sentences are documentation obligations (A.1 items 132/133), and neither is discharged.

rows.expected: TOP-LEVEL must not report a COBOL element the operating environment did not activate; the recorded edge is a host that enters the run unit WITHOUT ProgramTable.RunMain
rows.actual: THE EDGE IS PROBEABLE AND IT REPRODUCES. PowerShell 7.6.4 on this machine runs on .NET 10.0.10, so the runtime's PUBLIC host surface can be driven directly with NOTHING built: load Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll and the emitted assembly, call ProgramRegistry.Reset(), the emitted `public static class __CobolModule`'s Register(), then ProgramRegistry.CallProgram(...) -- RunMain is never called, so ModuleStack.PushMain never runs and frame 0 is an ordinary CALLed frame. rxh1 host-entered prints `H-TOP=[RXH1]`, identical to the CLI control. rxh2 makes it decisive: the CLI control, where the operating environment activates RXH2A, prints `B-TOP=[RXH2A]`; the SAME assembly host-entered at RXH2B prints `B-TOP=[RXH2B]` with `B-STK=[RXH2B; ]`, RXH2A never activated. TOP-LEVEL simply names whichever frame was pushed first. A second observable in the same run: `B-ACT=[ ]` -- the single space r5 reserves for a COBOL MAIN program -- is returned for a program that is not a main program.
rows.derivation: 15.65.4 r10 (spec line 32488): "If the TOP-LEVEL keyword is specified, then the returned value is the name of the runtime element that was activated by the operating environment to initiate the currently running run unit or application." The rule keys on HOW frame 0 came to exist. rows.derivation: SS15.67.4 1) 'The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1.' (--check OK), with no channel qualification. SS15.4.1 licenses implementor-defined characteristics ONLY 'when native arithmetic is in effect'; otherwise 'the returned value ... is contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect', and SS8.8.1.5.2 gives the SDIDI 'a maximum precision of 34 decimal digits'. So under standard-decimal a 7-fraction-digit value must survive, and a 34-digit integer (the exact bound SS15.67.3 r4 admits) must be representable.

rows.expected: The returned value is greater than or equal to zero and LESS THAN ONE. On a fixed-point receiver the emitter's quantization may not turn a value strictly below 1 into exactly 1: FUNCTION SQRT(0.999999999) = 0.9999999995 must not become 1.000000000 in a PIC 9V9(9) receiver, and no RANDOM draw may ever land at or above 1.
rows.actual: The quantization defect reproduces, and I isolated the emitter as the cause. p7541e (--std 2023, one value, three receiver shapes): 'FLOATRCV=0.9999999995' (COMP-2 receiver, unquantized, correctly < 1) / 'FIXED9  =1000000000' (PIC 9V9(9) - EXACTLY 1.000000000, the bound broken) / 'FIXED12 =0999999999500' (PIC 9V9(12), threshold not yet reached). p7541a corroborates the neighbour: 'SQRT9 =1000000000' vs 'SQRT8 =0999999999'. Source unchanged at HEAD: CobolIntrinsics.cs:171 'return (Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);' and IntrinsicRenderer.cs:335 wrapping every fixed-receiver call in FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:86/92-96 (Random) carries no clamp. DIRECT RANDOM SAMPLING CONFIRMS THE BUCKET IS UNREACHABLE BY SAMPLING, WHICH IS WHY THE SHARED-PATH PROBE IS THE EVIDENCE: p7541b (20,000 draws from seed 1, PIC 9V9(9) receiver) gives 'MAXSEEN=0999985055' / 'GE1HITS=000000', and p7541c (200,000 draws into a COARSER PIC 9V9(4) receiver) also gives 'GE1HITS=000000' - because ws is max(Receiver.Scale, 9), the coarse receiver does NOT lower the threshold, so ~5e-10 per draw is the ceiling on reachability at every receiver width.
rows.derivation: 15.75.4 1) 'The returned value is greater than or equal to zero and less than one.' (cite.py --check 15.75.4 -> OK §15.75.4 1)). 'Less than one' is strict, so any code path that can yield exactly 1 for a value the generator produced below 1 violates it; the violation is in the emitter, not the generator, which makes SQRT - sharing RenderFloat and the single FromDouble quantization point with RANDOM - a legitimate and in fact SHARPER witness, since it lets the boundary be hit deterministically. The three-receiver probe is what turns that from an argument into a measurement: the same mathematical value is < 1 through the float receiver and exactly 1 through the scale-9 fixed receiver, so the difference is entirely the quantization the rule forbids.
rows.probe: p7541e.cob (PROGRAM-ID PRD7541E): '01 WSFLT USAGE COMP-2. 01 WS9 PIC 9V9(9). 01 WS12 PIC 9V9(12).' each COMPUTEd from 'FUNCTION SQRT(0.999999999)' and displayed. p7541a.cob (PRD7541A): SQRT(0.999999999) vs SQRT(0.999999998) into PIC 9V9(9). p7541b.cob (PRD7541B): seed 1 then 20,000 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM' with a running max and a 'IF R NOT < 1' counter. p7541c.cob (PRD7541C): 200,000 draws into PIC 9V9(4) with the same counter. Command: cobol.exe <f>.cob --std 2023 -o <f>.dll --run.
rows.mechanism: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat wraps every fixed-point-receiver intrinsic result in CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = Math.Max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble ends in (Int128)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) - a generic away-from-zero rounding with no range-bounded-function clamp, so the top half-ulp of the [0,1) codomain rounds out of the codomain.
rows.attribution: unattributed

rows.expected: The implementor shall SPECIFY the subset of argument-1 values yielding distinct sequences, and that subset shall include 0 through at least 32767. Annex A.1 item 145 makes it a required item that shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation, so conformance needs the written entry as well as the behaviour - a docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 row naming the subset.
rows.actual: The behaviour still holds; the DOCUMENTATION is still absent, which is the half the PARTIAL verdict rested on. Behaviour re-measured, p7543a (--std 2023): 'S0        =0726243270' / 'S2POW31   =0726243270' (seed 2147483648 aliases onto 0 - the latitude rule 3 permits, provided the subset is specified) / 'S1        =0248668584' / 'S32767    =0036513305' / 'S32766    =0514087991' - the required-subset endpoints and their neighbours give distinct first values. Documentation: grep of docs/CONFORMANCE.md finds NO Annex A.1 item 145 row, no occurrence of '32767', no occurrence of 'distinct sequ', and no §15.75.4 reference anywhere in the file. The only RANDOM row is item 144 at line 336, which covers a DIFFERENT rule - §15.75.3 r4, the unseeded first-reference seed value (added 2026-08-09 with a GnuCOBOL survey). So the neighbouring obligation was documented and this one was not.
rows.derivation: 15.75.4 3) 'The implementor shall specify the subset of the domain of argument-1 values that will yield distinct sequences of pseudo-random numbers. This subset shall include the values from 0 through at least 32767.' (read directly at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.75.4). 'Shall specify' is an obligation on the IMPLEMENTOR's documentation, not on the generated program - which is why the behaviour passing does not discharge it, and why Annex A.1 item 145 ('shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') is the operative requirement. The rule is discharged only by a CONFORMANCE.md row naming a subset that has actually been measured.
rows.probe: p7543a.cob (PROGRAM-ID PRD7543A): 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(0)' / RANDOM(2147483648) / RANDOM(1) / RANDOM(32767) / RANDOM(32766), each displayed from '01 R PIC 9V9(9)'. Command: cobol.exe p7543a.cob --std 2023 -o p7543a.dll --run. Documentation half: grep -n -i "RANDOM" docs/CONFORMANCE.md (one hit, line 336, item 144 / §15.75.3 r4) and grep -n "145\|distinct sequ\|32767" docs/CONFORMANCE.md and grep -n "15\.75\.4" docs/CONFORMANCE.md (both empty).
rows.mechanism: The 2026-08-09 CONFORMANCE.md pass added Annex A.1 item 144 for §15.75.3 r4 (the unseeded seed) and stopped there, so item 145 - the DISTINCT-SEQUENCE SUBSET for §15.75.4 r3 - has no row in section 7; the register is hand-maintained per Annex item rather than driven from a §-to-item index, so an adjacent rule in the same function got the entry and this one silently did not.
