rows.expected: For any legal argument-1 that is a character string of length n, a character string of length n with position j holding argument-1's position n-j+1. An alphanumeric GROUP item is class and category alphanumeric per 8.5.2.1, so 15.78.3 r1 admits it and r1 must return its reversed image.
rows.actual: Two of the note's three failing shapes are FIXED, the third still reproduces. FIXED: P78401 EXIT=0 prints RV-SP=[        ], RV-AL=[BA      ] (correctly reversing ALL "AB") and RV-QT=["       ] - the BoundFigurative and BoundAllLiteral Loud arms are gone. STILL LIVE: P78402 compiles EXIT=0 and then terminates with 'Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... whole-group image of \'G2\' with a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf — the Tier-C byte island (no whole-group character image), deferred; COBOLNET_DESIGN §4.2' (exit -532462766). No returned value is produced, so r1 is violated for that argument shape.
rows.derivation: 15.78.4 r1 verbatim: 'If argument-1 is a character string of length n, the returned value is a character string of length n such that for 1 <= j <= n, the character in position j of the returned value is the character from position n – j + 1 of argument-1.' The rule is unconditional on the argument's internal composition; 8.5.2.1 gives an alphanumeric group item class AND category alphanumeric, which 15.78.3 r1 admits, so G2 - a group of PIC X(3) plus PIC S9(4) COMP-5 - is a legal argument and r1 REQUIRES a returned value of its image length. A run-time abort returns nothing at all. For the two fixed shapes, 8.3.3.6.4 GR3 b/c fix the lengths (SPACE one character, ALL "AB" two) and r1 predicts ' ' and 'BA' - both observed.

rows.expected: Spot-check of a STILL-LIVE claim. §15.79.4 1) makes the returned value ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) with S carrying the seconds subfield's fraction, so at ten fractional digits ("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000") must return +45296.3000000000. Nine digits is the §15.3.3.2 floor and must be exact as a control.
rows.actual: REPRODUCES UNCHANGED. s5chk.cob -> F10=[+45295.8705032704] where +45296.3000000000 is required; the control F9=[+45296.300000000] is exact. The observed error is precisely the int32 wrap the prober names: 3000000000 - 2^32 = -1294967296, i.e. 45296.3 - 1.2949672960 = 45295.8705032704 at scale 10. The prober's STILL-LIVE is not over-charged, and the wrap begins at exactly the first width above the nine-digit floor.
rows.derivation: §15.79.4 1) (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, '15.79.4 Returned Value rule') 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows: ((H * 3600) + (M * 60) + S) where H is the portion of argument-2 corresponding to the hours subfield of the format in argument-1, M is the portion ... and S is the portion of argument-2 corresponding to the seconds subfield'. S is the whole seconds subfield including its decimal fraction (§15.3.3.2), whose maximum width is implementor-defined but not less than nine; 12x3600 + 34x60 + 56 = 45296, plus the stated fraction .3.
rows.probe: s5chk.cob (RSF7941CHK): `01 WA PIC +9(5).9(10).` with ("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000") and `01 WB PIC +9(5).9(9).` with ("hhmmss.sssssssss", "123456300000000"). Command: cobol.exe s5chk.cob --std 2023 -o s5chk.dll --run. Output: F10=[+45295.8705032704] / F9=[+45296.300000000].
rows.mechanism: Confirmed as the prober describes: CobolDate.Analyze accumulates every subfield through a local 32-bit `int val` and then assigns it into the already-64-bit `frac`, so the digits wrap modulo 2^32 before the widening; the observed value matches that arithmetic exactly at the first width past nine. The fix is a wide accumulator, not a clamp on the format - and it is now MORE urgent than when recorded, because CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 202 documents a maximum of 18.
rows.attribution: n/a (STILL-LIVE).

rows.expected: SS15.8.4 r1 requires the returned value to be <= pi = 3.14159265358979323846. A COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates toward zero (SS14.7.4.3 GR2), so a conforming temporary can put at most 3.141592653 into PIC S9(1)V9(9) and at most 3.14159265358979323 into PIC S9(1)V9(17).
rows.actual: `ACOS9 =314159265D` (D = 4 positive) = 3.141592654, over pi by ~4.1e-10; `ACOS17=31415926535897932H` (H = 8 positive) = 3.14159265358979328, over pi by ~4.2e-17. Both exceed the largest image an in-bound temporary could truncate to, so the temporary itself exceeds pi. The prober's finding reproduces verbatim.
rows.derivation: SS15.8.4 1) verbatim from line 30078: 'The returned value is the approximation of the arccosine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to pi.' SS15.4.1 (line 29777) grants latitude over 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value', not permission to leave a stated closed interval; 3.141592653 is representable at scale 9 and satisfies r1.

rows.mechanism: Emitter - `IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat` quantizes the fixed-point-receiver arm through `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble` at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9) with round-to-NEAREST, which carries pi*10^ws up past a closed normative endpoint; the quantizer has no knowledge of the function's declared interval.

rows.expected: Under OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL, COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ANNUITY(0.05 10) shall compile and return the 15.9.4 EAE evaluated in the 8.8.1.5 standard-decimal intermediate (0.129504574... into PIC 9V9(9)).
rows.actual: rf17a (RF17A, --std 2023, exit 70): 'error COBOLNET0899: FUNCTION ANNUITY under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL is recognized but not yet implemented: 15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to equal the equivalent arithmetic expression evaluated in the standard-decimal intermediate (8.8.1.5), and this function's native IEEE-double evaluation cannot honor that equality'. Legal COBOL still turned away; the diagnostic text now names the rule it is failing, which is honest staging but is still a loud reject.
rows.derivation: 15.4.1 read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 29793-29795: 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified: 1) the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression.' No staging latitude - 15.4.1's implementor-defined escapes are scoped to native arithmetic and to implementor-defined arguments/sub-expressions.
rows.probe: rf17a.cob (RF17A): OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. / 01 R PIC 9V9(9). / COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ANNUITY(0.05 10). cmd: cobol.exe rf17a.cob --std 2023 -o rf17a.dll --run
variations: independently authored program (not the prober's pa04a)
rows.mechanism: Binder staging gate: IntrinsicBinder's standard-arithmetic gate still stages ANNUITY behind COBOLNET0899 - the 15.9.4 EAE is not evaluated in the CobolDec intermediate, so the whole standard-mode leg of the returned-value rule is unimplemented rather than wrong.

rows.expected: Under SR6 the '(' after a REPOSITORY-declared, argument-permitting intrinsic written WITHOUT the word FUNCTION is its ARGUMENT LIST, so `UPPER-CASE(1:2)` is an argument list holding '1:2' - not an argument - and must be rejected AS AN ARGUMENT-LIST ERROR (the COBOLNET1543 SR6 message the FUNCTION-keyword form already emits), never as an undefined data-name.
rows.actual: ZSL01A -> `error COBOLNET1639: 'UPPER-CASE(1:2)' is not defined - no declaration in this source element gives the name 'UPPER-CASE' ... (ISO 8.4.2.1)`. The reference is rejected, but through the ordinary unresolved-name path, exactly as the note recorded. The RANDOM half of the record is FIXED: ZSL01E (`REPOSITORY. FUNCTION RANDOM INTRINSIC.` + `MOVE RANDOM (1:4) TO T`) now draws the SR6 message `error COBOLNET1543: 'RANDOM (.)' - the '(' after the name of a function that takes arguments is ALWAYS its argument list (ISO 8.4.3.2 SR6) ...`, identical to the FUNCTION-keyword form (ZSL01F), and ZSL01C (`COMPUTE WS-N = RANDOM (A)`) compiles and runs, so the PB9 'RANDOM cannot be written keyword-omitted at all' claim no longer holds.
rows.derivation: SR6 quoted verbatim from specs/ISO_COBOL.md 8.4.3.2.3 rule 6: "If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows function-prototype-name-1 or intrinsic-function-name-1, the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments." UPPER-CASE's definition permits arguments (15.97.2 takes argument-1) and the REPOSITORY paragraph declares it, so SR2 makes the keyword-omitted reference legal syntax and SR6 fixes the reading of the '(': it opened the argument list. 'start:length' is not an argument (SR8), so the construct is in error - but the error SR6 dictates is about the argument list, which is precisely the COBOLNET1543 message the code already owns (IntrinsicBinder.ResultRefMod). Read alongside the compiler's OWN gate: KeywordOmittedFunction returns null at `if (!catalogued || sig.MinArgs != 0) return null;` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:284), so any function with MinArgs > 0 never reaches ResultRefMod on this route.
rows.probe: ZSL01A: `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION UPPER-CASE INTRINSIC.` / `01 WS-A PIC X(6) VALUE "abcdef".` / `DISPLAY UPPER-CASE(1:2).` -- cobol.exe z01a.cob --std 2023 -o z01a.dll --run. Controls: ZSL01D `DISPLAY UPPER-CASE(WS-A)(1:3).` -> `ABC` (the legal two-suffix form still binds); ZSL01B `DISPLAY FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(1:2).` -> COBOLNET1504 'takes 1 argument(s); 0 given' (the FUNCTION-keyword form ALSO fails to reach the SR6 message for a MinArgs>0 function - it read the group as a ref-mod and reported arity); ZSL01E/ZSL01F the RANDOM pair above.
variations: keyword-omitted vs FUNCTION-keyword form
MinArgs=0 function (RANDOM) vs MinArgs>0 function (UPPER-CASE)
legal two-suffix `name(args)(start:len)` control
DISPLAY and MOVE statement contexts
rows.mechanism: Binder, IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction: the arm that routes a captured depth-0-colon group to ResultRefMod is gated on `sig.MinArgs != 0` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:284), so the SR6 argument-list reading is applied only to zero-argument-capable intrinsics and every MinArgs>0 name falls through to the unresolved-data-name path - the same two-arm dispatch, with the second arm unfixed.
